note: 预先编写；英文题目和选项精确匹配后使用，仅提交后显示。

entries.prompt: What is Yoshi’s hometown known for?
options: Its rice exports and softball teams.
Its green tea and clementines.
Its agricultural high school.
Its annual cherry blossom parties.
entries.promptZh: Yoshi 的家乡因什么而闻名？
optionsZh: 当地的大米出口和垒球队。
当地的绿茶和小柑橘。
当地的农业高中。
当地每年的赏樱聚会。

entries.prompt: Which statement best restates Yoshi’s connection with earlier generations?
options: He followed a family pattern in both place and occupation.
He returned to the town after years overseas.
He shared his ancestors’ birthplace but rejected their work.
He left farming to study family history.
entries.promptZh: 哪一项最准确地改述了 Yoshi 与前几代人的联系？
optionsZh: 他在居住地点和职业上都延续了家族的生活模式。
他在海外生活多年后回到了小镇。
他与祖先生于同一地点，却拒绝从事他们的工作。
他离开农业，转而研究家族历史。

entries.prompt: What did Yoshi do after about one year of agricultural high school?
options: He became a farmer.
He married a woman from his school.
He moved to a neighbouring town.
He joined a softball league professionally.
entries.promptZh: 读了约一年农业高中后，Yoshi 做了什么？
optionsZh: 他成为了一名农民。
他娶了一位同校女子。
他搬到了邻近的小镇。
他加入了职业垒球联赛。

entries.prompt: What does the passage explicitly say about Yoshi’s close friends?
options: They are mainly people he met through his wife.
They are the same friends he has known since elementary school.
They returned to his town only after he turned fifty.
They organise professional softball tours for him.
entries.promptZh: 片段明确说，Yoshi 的亲密朋友有什么特点？
optionsZh: 他们主要是他通过妻子认识的人。
他们仍是他从小学起就认识的同一批朋友。
他们直到他年过五十才回到他的小镇。
他们为他组织职业垒球巡回比赛。

entries.prompt: In “the path laid out by his ancestors”, what does “path” refer to?
options: The physical route from Kyushu to Tokyo.
A sequence of trips organised by neighbours.
A road connecting farms and hot springs.
An established way of living passed through the family.
entries.promptZh: 在“祖先铺设的道路”中，“道路”指什么？
optionsZh: 从九州到东京的实际路线。
邻居组织的一系列旅行。
连接农场与温泉的道路。
家族世代传承的一种既定生活方式。

entries.prompt: How soon after his eighteenth birthday did the narrator leave for college?
options: On the day of his eighteenth birthday.
Eighteen months after his birthday.
Exactly eighteen days after his birthday.
After spending eighteen years in Tokyo.
entries.promptZh: 叙述者在十八岁生日多久后离开家乡上大学？
optionsZh: 在十八岁生日当天。
生日后十八个月。
生日后恰好十八天。
在东京度过十八年之后。

entries.prompt: What enabled the author to study abroad in Maine during college?
options: An invitation from his girlfriend in Boston.
A job with Japan’s Ministry of Education.
A place on a neighbourhood association trip.
A scholarship from Rotary International.
entries.promptZh: 大学期间，什么使作者得以前往缅因州留学？
optionsZh: 波士顿女友的邀请。
日本文部省的一份工作。
邻里协会旅行的一个名额。
国际扶轮提供的奖学金。

entries.prompt: Which event occurred before the author began the programme in Maine?
options: He attended a summer English programme in New York City.
He reunited with his girlfriend in Tokyo.
He completed a year of graduate study in Boston.
He decided to stop learning English.
entries.promptZh: 在开始缅因州的课程之前，作者经历了什么？
optionsZh: 他在纽约市参加了暑期英语课程。
他与东京的女友复合。
他在波士顿完成了一年研究生学习。
他决定停止学习英语。

entries.prompt: What contrast is introduced by “Yet” in the account of the summer programme?
options: He wanted a relationship but decided to study instead.
He hoped only to improve his English but unexpectedly fell in love.
He disliked Boston but visited it for academic research.
He planned to stay in Tokyo but found a job in Maine.
entries.promptZh: 在暑期课程的叙述中，“Yet”引出了什么转折？
optionsZh: 他原本想恋爱，后来却决定学习。
他原本只想提高英语，却意外坠入爱河。
他不喜欢波士顿，却为了学术研究前往那里。
他计划留在东京，却在缅因州找到工作。

entries.prompt: Why did the author take a bus to Boston every weekend?
options: To attend his own graduate classes there.
To return to Tokyo at the end of each week.
To begin his year in Lewiston.
To visit the woman who was starting graduate school there.
entries.promptZh: 作者为什么每个周末都乘巴士去波士顿？
optionsZh: 去那里参加自己的研究生课程。
每周末返回东京。
开始在刘易斯顿的一年生活。
看望将在那里开始研究生学习的那位女子。

entries.prompt: What contrast is introduced by “Though” in the passage?
options: He always planned to study in the U.S., but eventually refused to return.
His earlier plans excluded U.S. graduate study, but he later wanted to return.
He intended to work in Tokyo and therefore never changed his plans.
His original goal was to work for the U.S. Ministry of Education.
entries.promptZh: 片段中的“Though”引出了什么对照？
optionsZh: 他一直计划赴美读研，最终却拒绝回去。
较早的计划没有赴美读研，但后来他决心返回。
他打算在东京工作，因此从未改变计划。
他原先的目标是在美国教育部工作。

entries.prompt: What does “for good” mean in the author’s account of leaving Japan?
options: For the summer programme.
Permanently.
For the benefit of his hometown.
For a better-paid government job.
entries.promptZh: 作者叙述离开日本时，“for good”是什么意思？
optionsZh: 为了参加暑期课程。
永久地。
为了家乡的利益。
为了得到一份薪资更高的政府工作。

entries.prompt: What is explicitly stated about the author’s two children?
options: They were both born on Staten Island.
They were born to different mothers.
They were born in two different cities.
They were born before he met the Korean woman.
entries.promptZh: 片段明确说，作者的两个孩子有什么情况？
optionsZh: 他们都出生于斯塔滕岛。
他们的母亲不是同一个人。
他们出生于两座不同的城市。
他们出生在作者遇到那位韩国女子之前。

entries.prompt: What chiefly occupies the author’s thoughts three decades after leaving home?
options: Whether his father should have changed his occupation.
Which of his former cities was the most comfortable.
Why his life and his father’s took such different courses.
How to persuade his children to return to Japan.
entries.promptZh: 离家三十年后，作者主要思考什么？
optionsZh: 父亲是否本该改变职业。
自己曾居住的哪座城市最舒适。
为什么自己与父亲的人生走上如此不同的道路。
如何说服孩子们回到日本。

entries.prompt: How does “on the other hand” organise the comparison?
options: It contrasts the father’s predictable comforts with the author’s more stressful life.
It shows that father and son share the same annual routine.
It attributes the father’s comfort to the author’s professional success.
It describes the father changing from a comfortable life to a stressful one.
entries.promptZh: “on the other hand”怎样组织这段比较？
optionsZh: 对照父亲可预期的安稳舒适与作者更有压力的生活。
说明父子拥有相同的年度生活安排。
把父亲的舒适归因于作者的职业成功。
描述父亲从舒适生活变得压力重重。

entries.prompt: Why does the author suggest he could not have lived exactly like his father?
options: He had an especially strong desire to explore beyond home.
His father had asked him to leave the town.
He found all friendship with old classmates uninteresting.
He was certain a stable life would make everyone unhappy.
entries.promptZh: 作者为什么认为自己无法完全过上父亲那样的生活？
optionsZh: 他有特别强烈的愿望，想探索家乡以外的世界。
父亲曾要求他离开小镇。
他觉得所有与老同学的友谊都毫无趣味。
他确信稳定的生活会使所有人不幸福。

entries.prompt: How has the author’s response to the choice between staying and going changed?
options: He now finds leaving easier than he did at graduation.
He has always found the choice equally difficult.
A once straightforward choice has become increasingly difficult.
He now rejects leaving because The Clash advised him to stay.
entries.promptZh: 作者对留下还是离开的抉择，反应发生了什么变化？
optionsZh: 如今离开比毕业时更容易。
他一直觉得这个抉择同样困难。
曾经简单的选择变得越来越困难。
如今他拒绝离开，因为 The Clash 劝他留下。

entries.prompt: Which priorities distinguish the two kinds of people described here?
options: Some favour stability, while others welcome adventure.
Some value academic research, while others reject it.
Some preserve old friendships, while others avoid friendship.
Some ask the question once, while others never ask it.
entries.promptZh: 这里描述的两类人，在优先考虑的事情上有何不同？
optionsZh: 一些人倾向稳定，另一些人欢迎冒险。
一些人重视学术研究，另一些人排斥研究。
一些人维系老朋友，另一些人回避友谊。
一些人只问过一次这个问题，另一些人从未问过。

entries.prompt: What is the function of the paired alternatives such as “stable” and “mobile”?
options: To establish choices whose trade-offs raise the question of a good life.
To rank all mobile lives as morally superior.
To show that the author has abandoned psychological research.
To demonstrate that all readers have already made the same choice.
entries.promptZh: “稳定”与“流动”等成对选择起什么作用？
optionsZh: 列出需要权衡的选择，由此提出什么是美好生活的问题。
把所有流动的人生都评为道德上更优越。
说明作者已经放弃心理学研究。
证明所有读者都已作出同样的选择。

entries.prompt: How does the author plan to investigate what makes a good life?
options: By relying exclusively on philosophical definitions.
By using psychological research supplemented by cultural examples.
By replacing psychological data with personal opinions.
By treating literary stories as controlled experiments.
entries.promptZh: 作者计划如何探究什么构成美好生活？
optionsZh: 完全依靠哲学定义。
运用心理学研究，并辅以文化领域的例子。
用个人意见取代心理学数据。
把文学故事视为受控实验。

entries.prompt: What does “first” indicate about the question “What is a good life?”?
options: It has already been answered conclusively.
It will replace every later question in the book.
It should be postponed until the end of the discussion.
It is a starting point the discussion needs to address.
entries.promptZh: “first”说明“什么是美好生活”这个问题在讨论中处于什么位置？
optionsZh: 这个问题已有定论。
它将取代书中所有后续问题。
应该把它推迟到讨论结束。
它是讨论首先需要处理的起点。

entries.prompt: Why is Donna Tartt’s question included?
options: To prove that self-sacrifice prevents regret.
To report the results of an experiment about generosity.
To frame a tension between personal happiness and making others happy.
To establish that writers reject all forms of happiness.
entries.promptZh: 为什么引用唐娜·塔特提出的问题？
optionsZh: 证明自我牺牲能避免后悔。
报告一项关于慷慨的实验结果。
呈现个人幸福与让他人幸福之间的张力。
证明作家反对一切形式的幸福。

entries.prompt: Why does the author ask about freedom and career goals?
options: To prove that freedom and career success are identical.
To invite consideration of possible sources of personal happiness.
To announce the measured results of a career survey.
To conclude that career goals necessarily prevent happiness.
entries.promptZh: 作者为什么询问自由和职业目标？
optionsZh: 证明自由与事业成功完全相同。
邀请读者思考个人幸福可能来自哪里。
公布一项职业调查测得的结果。
断定职业目标必然妨碍幸福。

entries.prompt: What example does the author give of a decision he calls selfish?
options: Taking his sons out of university to travel.
Refusing a job because it involved moving.
Moving to New York City for a prestigious university job.
Sending his sons to a beach resort without him.
entries.promptZh: 作者举了哪个自称自私的决定作为例子？
optionsZh: 让儿子们退大学去旅行。
因为需要搬家而拒绝工作。
为了名校的一份工作搬到纽约市。
让儿子们独自去海滨度假村。

entries.prompt: What was the outcome of the author’s decision to maximise his own happiness by moving?
options: His father decided to move to the same city.
His sons immediately became happier at their new school.
He concluded that career moves never benefit anyone.
He did not find himself happier in the end.
entries.promptZh: 作者为最大化个人幸福而搬家，结果如何？
optionsZh: 父亲决定搬到同一座城市。
儿子们在新学校立即变得更幸福。
他断定职业变动永远不会使任何人获益。
最终，他并没有发现自己更幸福。

entries.prompt: Which statement preserves the author’s degree of certainty about his father’s decision?
options: He suggests, rather than establishes, that his father stayed to please others.
He proves that his father moved solely to earn more money.
He states that his father was unable to find work elsewhere.
He confirms that his mother ordered his father to remain.
entries.promptZh: 哪一说法保留了作者谈论父亲决定时的确定程度？
optionsZh: 他提出父亲可能为了让别人幸福而留下，并未把动机确定下来。
他证明父亲搬家完全为了多赚钱。
他断言父亲无法在其他地方找到工作。
他证实母亲命令父亲留下。

entries.prompt: Which paraphrase best matches the passage’s comparison of happiness-seeking strategies?
options: Trying to make oneself happy never succeeds.
Helping others guarantees permanent happiness for every individual.
The passage attributes happiness only to earning more money.
Seeking others’ happiness can benefit oneself, while a self-focused pursuit can fail.
entries.promptZh: 哪一改写最符合本段对追求幸福方式的比较？
optionsZh: 设法让自己幸福从来不会成功。
帮助别人保证每个人永久幸福。
本段把幸福完全归因于赚更多的钱。
追求他人的幸福可以使自己受益，而只求自己幸福有时会失败。

entries.prompt: How certain is the author about why his father has been happy?
options: He offers adjusted expectations as a possible explanation.
He identifies the father’s income as the only proven cause.
He says family tradition has no possible relevance.
He reports that his father was experimentally assigned to lower expectations.
entries.promptZh: 作者对父亲为何幸福的解释有多确定？
optionsZh: 他把调整期待作为一种可能的解释。
他认定父亲的收入是唯一得到证实的原因。
他说家族传统不可能有任何关系。
他报告父亲被实验分配到降低期待的条件中。

entries.prompt: What issue does the question about “a life without regrets” open up?
options: Whether the father has abandoned his family tradition.
Whether self-sacrifice and virtue necessarily prevent regret.
Whether the mother earned more than the father.
Whether all meaningful lives are financially successful.
entries.promptZh: 关于“没有遗憾的人生”的设问，引出了什么问题？
optionsZh: 父亲是否放弃了家庭传统。
自我牺牲和美德是否一定能避免遗憾。
母亲是否比父亲挣得更多。
所有有意义的人生是否都在经济上成功。

entries.prompt: Which contrast about regret does the author make?
options: Action tends to be regretted in the short term, inaction in the long run.
People regret inaction only when they are young.
Action and inaction cause identical regrets at every stage.
Long-term regret is always caused by self-sacrifice.
entries.promptZh: 作者对两种后悔作了什么对照？
optionsZh: 短期更容易后悔采取行动，长期更容易后悔没有行动。
人们只有年轻时才会后悔没有行动。
在人生每个阶段，行动和不行动都会带来完全相同的后悔。
长期后悔总是由自我牺牲造成。

entries.prompt: What possible cost of self-sacrifice is identified in this sentence?
options: Missed opportunities may later become sources of regret.
Virtue invariably makes people financially poorer.
Every sacrifice leads to immediate public criticism.
Regret disappears once a person gives up opportunities.
entries.promptZh: 这句话指出自我牺牲可能付出什么代价？
optionsZh: 错过的机会日后可能成为遗憾的来源。
美德必然使人更贫穷。
每次牺牲都会立刻招致公开批评。
一旦放弃机会，遗憾就会消失。

entries.prompt: What risk of prioritising self-sacrifice is described?
options: People necessarily become unwilling to help others.
People always gain clearer personal ideals.
People may lose contact with their own wishes and feel less authentic.
People can no longer remember their childhood families.
entries.promptZh: 文中指出，优先选择自我牺牲可能有什么风险？
optionsZh: 人们必然变得不愿帮助他人。
人们总会更清楚自己的理想。
人们可能逐渐疏远自身愿望，觉得不再忠于自我。
人们再也记不起童年的家庭。

entries.prompt: How is Nel Wright’s choice used to illustrate the idea in this passage?
options: She rejects family expectations to pursue childhood adventures.
Her life provides experimental proof that marriage causes regret.
She sets aside adventurous dreams to meet expectations of being a wife and mother.
She persuades Sartre to change his definition of authenticity.
entries.promptZh: 本段怎样通过 Nel Wright 的选择来举例？
optionsZh: 她拒绝家庭期待，追逐儿时冒险梦想。
她的人生提供了婚姻导致遗憾的实验依据。
她搁置冒险梦想，去符合妻子和母亲角色的期待。
她说服萨特改变真实生活的定义。

entries.prompt: What role does the account of Oliver Sacks play here?
options: It establishes that Sartre conducted research on Sacks.
It shows that professional boundaries never matter.
It proves that depression is necessary for a valuable life.
It offers an example of an adventurous, experientially rich life despite hardship.
entries.promptZh: 这里对奥利弗·萨克斯的叙述起什么作用？
optionsZh: 证明萨特研究过萨克斯。
说明职业界限从来不重要。
证明抑郁是有价值人生的必要条件。
提供一个虽有艰难，却充满探索和丰富经历的人生例子。

entries.prompt: Why does Sacks’s life present a “quandary” for the author?
options: It was entirely free of emotional struggle.
It was admirable only because of financial success.
It shows that exploration necessarily cures depression.
Its admirable qualities are not fully captured by happiness or self-sacrifice.
entries.promptZh: 为什么 Sacks 的人生使作者感到现有概念难以解释？
optionsZh: 他完全没有情绪困扰。
他的人生只因财务成功而值得钦佩。
它说明探索必定能治愈抑郁。
幸福或自我牺牲都不能完整概括其中令人钦佩的品质。

entries.prompt: Who does the sentence credit with choosing the term “a psychologically rich life”?
options: Oliver Sacks and his publisher.
The author and his students.
The author’s father and neighbours.
An unnamed group of philosophers.
entries.promptZh: 这句话把“心理丰富的人生”这一术语的选定归于谁？
optionsZh: Oliver Sacks 和他的出版商。
作者及其学生。
作者的父亲和邻居。
一群未具名的哲学家。

entries.prompt: Which feature is central to the author’s definition of a psychologically rich life?
options: Diverse and interesting experiences that change one’s perspective.
A constant feeling of personal contentment.
Self-sacrifice as the single measure of a good life.
Unchanging routines that remove every surprise.
entries.promptZh: 作者定义的心理丰富人生，其核心特征是什么？
optionsZh: 多样、有趣且能改变个人视角的经历。
持续不断的个人满足感。
把自我牺牲作为美好生活的唯一标准。
消除一切意外、一成不变的日常。

entries.prompt: Why does the author compare psychological richness to dark chocolate?
options: To show that richness is a measure of food quality alone.
To recommend replacing sweet food with bitter food.
To claim that unpleasant experiences are always preferable.
To illustrate surprise, complexity and a mixture of qualities.
entries.promptZh: 作者为什么把心理丰富性比作黑巧克力？
optionsZh: 说明丰富性只衡量食物品质。
建议以苦味食物取代甜食。
声称不愉快的经历总是更好。
说明意外感、复杂性以及多种特质的混合。

entries.prompt: What does the phrase “a distinct multitude of flavors” suggest here?
options: A life containing a varied collection of experiences.
A diet made up mainly of different chocolates.
A life defined by repeatedly having one pleasant feeling.
A method of measuring food preferences over time.
entries.promptZh: “a distinct multitude of flavors”在这里暗示什么？
optionsZh: 一种由多样经历构成的人生。
一种主要由不同巧克力构成的饮食。
一种由反复体验单一愉快感受定义的人生。
一种长期测量食物偏好的方法。

entries.prompt: Why does the author introduce a detour into research history?
options: To abandon the question of why a new term is needed.
To argue that research on the good life has ended.
To explain the need for the new term through three research phases.
To rank three phases by the happiness of their researchers.
entries.promptZh: 作者为什么转向回顾研究史？
optionsZh: 放弃解释为什么需要新术语。
宣称关于美好生活的研究已经结束。
通过三个研究阶段解释为什么需要新术语。
按研究者的幸福程度给三个阶段排名。

entries.prompt: Which detail about Ed Diener is explicitly stated?
options: He coined the term psychological richness in 1984.
He was the author’s graduate advisor and published “Subjective Well-Being” in 1984.
He was the only researcher who had ever studied happiness.
He supervised the author’s high-school studies.
entries.promptZh: 关于 Ed Diener，哪项细节在原文中明确出现？
optionsZh: 他在 1984 年创造了心理丰富这一术语。
他是作者的研究生导师，并于 1984 年发表《Subjective Well-Being》。
他是唯一研究过幸福的人。
他指导作者的高中学习。

entries.prompt: What contribution is attributed to Ed Diener and his students?
options: Helping establish happiness as a legitimate topic of scientific study.
Proving that psychological richness and happiness are identical.
Creating the eudaimonic approach in 1989.
Replacing all research on hope and optimism with autobiography.
entries.promptZh: 文中将什么贡献归于埃德·迪纳及其学生？
optionsZh: 帮助确立幸福作为一个正当的科学研究主题。
证明心理丰富性与幸福完全相同。
在 1989 年创立实现论取向。
用自传取代所有希望与乐观方面的研究。

entries.prompt: What was positive psychology based on, according to this sentence?
options: Happiness research alone, excluding all related topics.
The study of material wealth rather than psychological states.
Only the study of psychological illness and its treatment.
The study of happiness together with topics such as hope, optimism, and flow.
entries.promptZh: 根据这句话，积极心理学建立在什么研究基础上？
optionsZh: 只有幸福研究，排除一切相关主题。
物质财富研究，而非心理状态研究。
只有心理疾病及其治疗研究。
幸福研究，以及希望、乐观、心流等相关主题的研究。

entries.prompt: Which combination belongs to Carol Ryff’s alternative model described here?
options: Autonomy, purpose, and personal growth.
Income, fame, and physical comfort.
Obedience, competition, and career status.
Pleasure, entertainment, and freedom from all duties.
entries.promptZh: 哪组要素属于这里描述的 Carol Ryff 的替代模型？
optionsZh: 自主性、目标感和个人成长。
收入、名气和身体舒适。
服从、竞争和职业地位。
愉悦、娱乐和免除所有责任。

entries.prompt: How does the passage distinguish the eudaimonic and hedonic approaches?
options: The former concerns money; the latter concerns social status.
The former was developed by Diener; the latter by Ryff.
The former is linked to a meaningful life; the latter to a happy life.
The former rejects personal growth; the latter requires self-sacrifice.
entries.promptZh: 文中如何区分实现论取向与享乐论取向？
optionsZh: 前者关注金钱，后者关注社会地位。
前者由迪纳提出，后者由里夫提出。
前者联系有意义的生活，后者联系幸福的生活。
前者反对个人成长，后者要求自我牺牲。

entries.prompt: What distinction is illustrated by the comparison between work and a break?
options: Workers are less engaged during work and happier during work.
Having an easy life necessarily makes life meaningful.
Greater happiness during breaks can coexist with greater engagement during work.
Work and breaks have identical effects on happiness and engagement.
entries.promptZh: 工作与休息的比较说明了什么区别？
optionsZh: 工作时投入更少，而且更幸福。
生活轻松必然使人生有意义。
休息时更幸福可以与工作时更投入同时存在。
工作和休息对幸福与投入的作用完全相同。

entries.prompt: What is the best summary of the debate described in this paragraph?
options: Researchers unanimously deny that happiness and meaning overlap.
Findings and interpretations differ about the distinction and overlap between happiness and meaning.
The debate has established epigenetic differences beyond dispute.
Every study shows that breaks are more meaningful than work.
entries.promptZh: 哪一项最能概括本段所述的争论？
optionsZh: 研究者一致否认幸福与意义有重叠。
对于幸福与意义的区别和重叠，研究结果及解释存在分歧。
争论已无可争议地确立了表观遗传差异。
每项研究都显示休息比工作更有意义。

entries.prompt: What has been disputed among the researchers described in this sentence?
options: Whether either happiness or meaning can ever be studied.
Which matters more: happiness or meaning.
Whether all people define happiness identically.
Which research method measures wealth most accurately.
entries.promptZh: 这句话中的研究者在争论什么？
optionsZh: 幸福或意义究竟能否被研究。
幸福和意义，哪一个更重要。
所有人对幸福的定义是否完全一样。
哪种研究方法能最准确地测量财富。

entries.prompt: What does the comparison with nature, nurture and growth mindset illustrate?
options: That genetic explanations of intelligence should replace all others.
That psychological richness determines intelligence.
That a third concept can broaden a discussion framed by two dimensions.
That happiness is irrelevant once richness is considered.
entries.promptZh: 以先天、后天和成长型思维作比较，说明什么？
optionsZh: 智力的遗传解释应当取代所有其他解释。
心理丰富性决定智力。
第三个概念能够拓宽原本由两个维度构成的讨论。
一旦考虑丰富性，幸福就无关紧要。

entries.prompt: Which belief is singled out as relevant to predicting intelligence and performance?
options: The belief that intelligence is determined entirely by income.
The belief that all people have already reached their potential.
The belief that performance cannot be studied scientifically.
The belief that intelligence can be improved.
entries.promptZh: 哪种观念被特别指出与预测智力和表现有关？
optionsZh: 智力完全由收入决定。
所有人都已经达到自己的潜能上限。
人的表现无法得到科学研究。
智力可以得到提高。

entries.prompt: Why did the author initially suggest hiring someone to repair the window?
options: He regarded himself as unskilled at practical repairs.
His son had already repaired every window in the house.
His wife wanted to replace the entire Victorian house.
The windows had never used sash cords.
entries.promptZh: 作者最初为什么建议请人修窗户？
optionsZh: 他认为自己不擅长动手维修。
儿子已经修好了房子里的每扇窗。
妻子想更换整座维多利亚式房子。
窗户从未使用过窗绳。

entries.prompt: What idea is expressed by “You can get better!”?
options: Improvement is possible only outside school.
A person’s present skill level can never change.
A person can develop abilities rather than remain at the current level.
Learning about a mindset guarantees immediate expert performance.
entries.promptZh: “You can get better!”表达了什么想法？
optionsZh: 只有在校外才可能进步。
一个人当前的技能水平永远不能改变。
人的能力可以发展，并非只能停留在当前水平。
学到一种思维模式便保证立刻成为专家。

entries.prompt: What effect did the son’s comment have on the author?
options: It persuaded him that only professionals can learn new skills.
It encouraged him to repair the window and improve his practical skills.
It made him abandon the idea that mindsets can change.
It caused his wife to hire a different handyman.
entries.promptZh: 儿子的评论对作者产生了什么影响？
optionsZh: 说服他相信只有专业人员才能学习新技能。
鼓励他修理窗户并提升动手能力。
使他放弃思维模式能够改变的想法。
使妻子另外雇了一名修理工。

entries.prompt: How does the author use the analogy with the growth mindset?
options: To claim that psychological richness has already replaced intelligence research.
To express hope that psychological richness will expand the idea of a good life.
To show that growth mindset and psychological richness are identical measures.
To prove that every new concept immediately improves everyone’s life.
entries.promptZh: 作者怎样运用与成长型思维的类比？
optionsZh: 断言心理丰富已取代智力研究。
表达心理丰富有望拓展美好生活概念的期待。
说明成长型思维和心理丰富是同一个指标。
证明每个新概念都会立刻改善所有人的生活。

entries.prompt: Which feature of happiness is introduced by the balloon comparison?
options: It grows permanently whenever a person has a new experience.
It measures the social impact of a person’s work.
It can be assessed only by observing physical balloons.
It is a subjective feeling that rises and falls.
entries.promptZh: 气球的比较首先引出了幸福的哪种特征？
optionsZh: 每有新经历就会永久增长。
它衡量一个人工作的社会影响。
只有观察真实气球才能评估它。
它是一种会起伏的主观感受。

entries.prompt: What change is marked by “But” in the balloon image?
options: The balloon becomes unaffected by its surroundings.
Bad weather is presented as the cause of smooth sailing.
Favourable conditions keep it high, whereas bad weather makes it deflate.
The passage shifts from a metaphor to results of a weather experiment.
entries.promptZh: 气球意象中的“But”标记了什么变化？
optionsZh: 气球不再受周围环境影响。
坏天气被说成是一帆风顺的原因。
有利条件使它高高飘起，而坏天气使它瘪下来。
从比喻转为报告天气实验结果。

entries.prompt: In these short statements, what does “Grounded and stuck” convey?
options: A state of being held down and unable to progress.
A feeling of rapid and effortless progress.
A successful arrival at a planned destination.
A decision to begin a new research project.
entries.promptZh: 在这两句短句中，“Grounded and stuck”表达什么状态？
optionsZh: 被困住、难以前进的状态。
迅速而轻松地向前发展的感受。
成功抵达预定目的地。
决定开始一个新的研究项目。

entries.prompt: What does the batting-average comparison suggest about happiness?
options: Only rare, spectacular achievements have lasting value.
Frequent small positive interactions can matter more than occasional major successes.
Happiness remains constant once a major goal is reached.
The size of each pleasant event is the only important factor.
entries.promptZh: 击球率的比较对幸福有什么启示？
optionsZh: 只有罕见而惊人的成就才有长久价值。
频繁的小型积极互动可能比偶尔的重大成功更重要。
达到一个重大目标后，幸福就保持不变。
每件愉快事件的强度是唯一重要因素。

entries.prompt: What is “the snag” in the discussion of happiness?
options: Sporting results cannot be measured.
William James rejects all pleasant experiences.
Happiness fluctuates and therefore offers insecure support.
Success is impossible in a prosperous life.
entries.promptZh: 讨论幸福时提到的“障碍”是什么？
optionsZh: 体育成绩无法测量。
威廉·詹姆斯拒绝所有愉快经历。
幸福会波动，因此不是稳固的支撑。
在富足生活中不可能成功。

entries.prompt: In the phrase “boils down to”, what is the author doing?
options: Claiming that every effort produces a clear legacy.
Explaining how a song was produced.
Reducing a complex idea to its central question.
Describing a process for removing negative emotions.
entries.promptZh: 使用“boils down to”时，作者在做什么？
optionsZh: 声称每份努力都能留下明确的遗产。
解释一首歌的制作过程。
把一个复杂概念归结为它的核心问题。
描述消除负面情绪的过程。

entries.prompt: When does the passage say it becomes harder to see the point of one’s life?
options: Whenever a person begins to care about the world.
When one’s efforts do not seem to make a clear difference.
Only after every long-term goal has been achieved.
As soon as one sees the fruits of one’s labour.
entries.promptZh: 本段说，什么时候会更难看清人生的意义所在？
optionsZh: 只要开始关心世界时。
当自己的努力似乎没有带来明确改变时。
只有在所有长期目标都达成以后。
一看到劳动成果时。

entries.prompt: What role does the imagined breakup play in this passage?
options: It reports a verified event in the singer’s biography.
It proves that romantic love always leads to failure.
It describes the results of a controlled relationship study.
It illustrates hypothetically how relationship-based meaning could feel lost.
entries.promptZh: 本段设想的分手起到什么作用？
optionsZh: 报告歌手生平中已经核实的事件。
证明爱情总是导致失败。
描述一项受控关系研究的结果。
以假设说明，依托一段关系的意义可能怎样失落。

entries.prompt: What does Tolstoy’s example suggest within this discussion?
options: External success and a loving family do not necessarily secure a sense of meaning.
Praise always prevents an existential crisis.
Tolstoy’s crisis was experimentally caused by writing novels.
Only people with financial losses question their lives.
entries.promptZh: 在这段讨论中，托尔斯泰的例子说明什么？
optionsZh: 外在成功与充满爱的家庭未必能保证意义感。
赞誉总能防止存在危机。
托尔斯泰的危机是由写小说的实验造成的。
只有遭受经济损失的人才会质疑人生。

entries.prompt: What does “precariousness” most nearly mean in this closing phrase?
options: The mathematical precision of meaning.
The unchangeable permanence of meaning.
The instability or vulnerability of meaning.
The complete absence of meaning in every life.
entries.promptZh: 结尾短语中的“precariousness”最接近什么意思？
optionsZh: 意义的数学精确性。
意义永不改变的持久性。
意义的不稳定性或脆弱性。
每个人的人生都完全没有意义。

entries.prompt: What distinguishes psychological richness in this passage?
options: It concerns accumulated experiences rather than an overall feeling or life’s point.
It is measured only by the amount of money a person earns.
It requires all experiences to produce the same pleasant feeling.
It is defined as having a single unchanging purpose throughout life.
entries.promptZh: 本段用什么特征区分心理丰富？
optionsZh: 它关注积累的经历，而非总体感受或人生目的。
它只用一个人挣多少钱来衡量。
它要求一切经历都带来同一种愉悦感受。
它被定义为终身拥有一个不变的目标。

entries.prompt: What relationship does the sentence establish between wealth and experiences?
options: Wealth is required before experiences can accumulate.
Both can accumulate, contributing to different kinds of richness.
Experiences can replace money in every financial transaction.
Accumulating wealth prevents psychological richness.
entries.promptZh: 这句话在财富与经历之间建立了什么关系？
optionsZh: 必须先有财富，经历才能积累。
二者都可以积累，分别形成不同的丰富。
经历能在所有金融交易中取代金钱。
积累财富会阻止心理丰富。

entries.prompt: How is psychological richness contrasted with happiness in the career-home-runs analogy?
options: Richness can be measured only in financial earnings.
Richness depends on winning every single game.
Richness accumulates through experiences rather than tracking a changing overall feeling.
Richness erases all earlier experiences after each new event.
entries.promptZh: 在职业生涯全垒打的类比中，心理丰富性与幸福有什么区别？
optionsZh: 丰富性只能通过收入来衡量。
丰富性取决于赢得每一场比赛。
丰富性通过经历不断积累，而非追踪不断变化的整体感受。
每个新事件都会使丰富性抹去所有先前经历。

entries.prompt: Who is described as better suited to a psychologically rich life?
options: Everyone, equally and without exception.
Only people who have accumulated great wealth.
People who are satisfied with never exploring anything new.
Curious people, more than people who are already content.
entries.promptZh: 原文说，什么人更适合心理丰富的人生？
optionsZh: 每个人都完全一样，毫无例外。
只有积累了巨额财富的人。
满足于永远不探索新事物的人。
比起已感到满足的人，更适合好奇的人。

entries.prompt: What does the author acknowledge about a psychologically rich life?
options: It is suitable only for people who are already happy.
It requires giving up every form of meaning.
It often lacks the comfort and security found in a happy or meaningful life.
It guarantees more security than any other life.
entries.promptZh: 作者承认心理丰富的人生有什么特点？
optionsZh: 它只适合已经幸福的人。
它要求放弃一切形式的意义。
它往往缺乏幸福或有意义生活所具有的舒适和安全感。
它保证比任何其他人生更安全。

entries.prompt: What paradox does the sentence identify?
options: Happiness and meaning necessarily eliminate every regret.
Unanswered questions always lead immediately to happiness.
The complacency encouraged by happiness and meaning can leave life incomplete.
Meaning is possible only when a person rejects happiness altogether.
entries.promptZh: 这句话指出了什么悖论？
optionsZh: 幸福和意义必然消除所有遗憾。
未解问题总会立刻带来幸福。
幸福和意义促生的自满，可能使人生仍不完整。
只有彻底拒绝幸福才可能有意义。

entries.prompt: What does “our lives are not zero-sum games” imply in this passage?
options: The three dimensions are always identical.
Happiness, meaning and richness can coexist in a person’s life.
A good life must choose richness instead of happiness.
Meaning is possible only after all curiosity disappears.
entries.promptZh: “我们的人生不是零和博弈”在本段意味着什么？
optionsZh: 三个维度始终完全相同。
幸福、意义和丰富性可以在同一个人的生活中共存。
美好生活必须选择丰富性而放弃幸福。
只有所有好奇心消失之后，意义才可能存在。

entries.prompt: Which conclusion stays within the passage’s claims about seeking new experiences?
options: It may help reduce regrets, but a regret-free life is expressed as a hope.
It guarantees that no reader will ever regret a decision.
It matters only after a person has reached every destination.
It requires abandoning the search for new knowledge.
entries.promptZh: 关于寻求新经历，哪个结论没有超出本段的说法？
optionsZh: 它可能有助于减少遗憾，但完全没有遗憾仍是一种期待。
它保证所有读者永远不后悔任何决定。
只有达成所有目的地以后，它才重要。
它要求放弃探索新知识。

entries.prompt: What alternatives does this question explicitly present?
options: Becoming wealthy or remaining poor.
Staying or going.
Studying alone or joining a research team.
Choosing happiness or rejecting all meaning.
entries.promptZh: 这个问句明确提出了哪两个选择？
optionsZh: 变富或保持贫穷。
留下或离开。
独自学习或加入研究团队。
选择幸福或拒绝一切意义。

entries.prompt: What can be inferred about people who choose to stay?
options: They must adopt the author’s pattern of repeated migration.
They cannot experience psychological richness without moving away.
They are guaranteed a completely regret-free life.
They may still gain interest and resilience through psychological richness.
entries.promptZh: 对于选择留下来的人，可以作出什么推断？
optionsZh: 他们必须采用作者不断迁移的生活模式。
不搬走就无法体验心理丰富性。
他们的人生一定完全没有后悔。
他们仍可能通过心理丰富性获得趣味与韧性。

entries.prompt: Which paraphrase preserves the meaning of “on the path toward psychological richness”?
options: They have already completed every stage of psychological development.
They can become psychologically rich only by travelling continuously.
They have proved that staying can never offer psychological richness.
They are already moving in the direction of psychological richness.
entries.promptZh: 哪个改写保留了“on the path toward psychological richness”的意思？
optionsZh: 他们已经完成心理发展的所有阶段。
他们只有不停旅行才能变得心理丰富。
他们已经证明留下永远不能带来心理丰富。
他们已经在朝心理丰富的方向前进。

entries.prompt: What do these three questions invite the reader to consider?
options: Which city has the highest average income.
Why happiness research must be abandoned completely.
The ingredients, examples, and distinctiveness of a psychologically rich life.
How all people can follow one identical life plan.
entries.promptZh: 这三个问题邀请读者思考什么？
optionsZh: 哪座城市的平均收入最高。
为什么必须完全放弃幸福研究。
心理丰富人生的要素、人物例子及其独特之处。
如何让所有人遵循完全相同的人生计划。

entries.prompt: What is the purpose of the questions at the end of this chapter?
options: To claim that indirect experiences have already been ruled out.
To preview issues that the rest of the book will explore.
To replace the earlier definition with a financial one.
To demonstrate that no research on richness exists.
entries.promptZh: 本章结尾的问题有什么目的？
optionsZh: 声称间接经历已被排除。
预告本书其余部分将探索的议题。
用财务方面的定义取代前面的定义。
证明丰富性方面不存在任何研究。

entries.prompt: Who is explicitly associated with the idea that happiness is “the ultimate goal of goals”?
options: William James.
Aristotle.
Ed Diener.
The survey respondents.
entries.promptZh: 文中明确把“幸福是所有目标的终极目标”这一观点与谁联系起来？
optionsZh: 威廉·詹姆斯。
亚里士多德。
埃德·迪纳。
调查受访者。

entries.prompt: According to the William James quotation, what drives much of human action and endurance?
options: The pursuit, preservation, and recovery of happiness.
The avoidance of every form of discomfort.
The aim of gaining money rather than happiness.
The wish to rank happiness below other concerns.
entries.promptZh: 根据 William James 的引述，什么推动着人们的许多行动和忍耐？
optionsZh: 追求、保持和重获幸福。
避免任何形式的不适。
追求金钱而不是幸福。
希望把幸福排在其他关切之后。

entries.prompt: What does the figure 69 percent refer to in Diener’s study?
options: Respondents who rated money as extremely important.
People whose health improved because they became happy.
Respondents who gave happiness the highest importance rating.
Respondents who ranked love and health above happiness.
entries.promptZh: Diener 的研究中，69% 这个数字指什么？
optionsZh: 认为金钱极其重要的受访者。
因为变得幸福而改善健康的人。
给幸福的重要性打出最高分的受访者。
认为爱情和健康比幸福更重要的受访者。

entries.prompt: What irony introduces the discussion of the happiness trap?
options: No one sees happiness as a worthwhile goal.
Happy people never help others.
Pursuing happiness blindly can sometimes produce unhappiness.
Public happiness always reflects inner experience.
entries.promptZh: 幸福陷阱的讨论以什么讽刺现象开场？
optionsZh: 没有人认为幸福是值得追求的目标。
幸福的人从来不帮助他人。
盲目追求幸福有时反而带来不幸福。
公开表现出的幸福总能反映内心体验。

entries.prompt: What contrast does the passage draw about Madison Holleran?
options: Her party photographs documented an entirely secure private life.
Her cheerful online image contrasted with a more uncertain reality.
Her unhappy online posts matched her troubled private life.
Her private life was secure although her posts suggested unhappiness.
entries.promptZh: 本段呈现了 Madison Holleran 的什么反差？
optionsZh: 她的聚会照片记录了完全安稳的私人生活。
她在网上的快乐形象与更不安稳的现实形成反差。
她网上的不快乐帖文与困扰重重的私人生活一致。
她的私人生活很安稳，尽管帖文显示她不快乐。

entries.prompt: What did Madison reveal to her sister about her social life?
options: She thought her friends had fewer social opportunities than she did.
She told her sister that her friends envied her social life.
She said her sister had a better social life than her friends.
She felt her social life compared unfavourably with her friends’.
entries.promptZh: Madison 向姐妹透露了自己对社交生活的什么感受？
optionsZh: 她认为朋友们的社交机会比自己少。
她告诉姐妹，朋友们羡慕自己的社交生活。
她说姐妹的社交生活比朋友们更好。
她觉得自己的社交生活比不上朋友们。

entries.prompt: What does the author stress when discussing Madison’s death?
options: Social comparison alone fully explains it.
A cheerful appearance rules out serious inner difficulties.
Its complexity cannot be reduced to one feeling of inferiority.
Her private feelings were objectively identical to her friends’.
entries.promptZh: 作者讨论 Madison 的死亡时强调什么？
optionsZh: 仅凭社会比较就能完整解释。
快乐的外表能排除严重内心困扰。
其复杂性不能简化为一种自卑感。
她的私人感受客观上与朋友完全相同。

entries.prompt: What does “14 out of 100,000” describe in the passage?
options: The rate of Americans dying by suicide in 2018.
The percentage increase from 2000 to 2018.
The number of adults reporting suicidal thoughts in 2020.
The proportion of all deaths attributed to suicide in 2018.
entries.promptZh: “每十万人中有十四人”在本段指什么？
optionsZh: 2018 年美国人死于自杀的比率。
2000 至 2018 年的百分比增幅。
2020 年报告自杀想法的成年人数量。
2018 年所有死亡中自杀所占的比例。

entries.prompt: Which interpretation matches the passage’s 2020 figures?
options: 1.2 million adults seriously considered suicide and 12.2 million attempted it.
Roughly one in twenty adults died by suicide that year.
The two figures count the same event in identical populations.
12.2 million adults seriously considered suicide, distinct from 1.2 million attempts.
entries.promptZh: 哪项解释符合本段的 2020 年数字？
optionsZh: 120 万成年人认真考虑自杀，1,220 万次为尝试。
当年约每二十名成年人中就有一人死于自杀。
两个数字统计的是相同人群中的同一种事件。
1,220 万成年人认真考虑自杀，有别于 120 万次自杀尝试。

entries.prompt: What issue does the question shift attention toward?
options: How to calculate an exact mortality rate.
Why someone experiencing suicidal thoughts felt pressure to appear happy.
Whether Madison ever experienced unhappiness.
Which public appearance proves an absence of inner struggle.
entries.promptZh: 这个问题把注意力转向什么？
optionsZh: 如何计算精确死亡率。
为什么有自杀想法的人仍感到必须表现快乐的压力。
Madison 是否曾经不快乐。
哪种公众表象能证明没有内心挣扎。

entries.prompt: What view of happiness is illustrated by the students’ responses?
options: Happiness is entirely unrelated to individual effort.
Happiness is an unavoidable outcome of chance alone.
Happiness is something achieved through effort and success.
Happiness is defined only by the absence of anger.
entries.promptZh: 学生的回答体现了怎样的幸福观？
optionsZh: 幸福与个人努力完全无关。
幸福只是运气必然带来的结果。
幸福可以通过努力和成功获得。
幸福只被定义为没有愤怒。

entries.prompt: What were college students asked to write about in the other study?
options: Aspects, features, or effects of happiness or unhappiness.
Only occasions when they won a competition.
Their predicted salary after graduation.
Reasons for ranking happiness above health.
entries.promptZh: 另一项研究要求大学生写什么？
optionsZh: 幸福或不幸福的方面、特征或影响。
仅写赢得比赛的场合。
毕业后预计能获得的薪水。
把幸福排在健康之前的理由。

entries.prompt: What association was found in the American college students’ responses?
options: Happiness was defined exclusively as inherited wealth.
Students agreed that sadness was a medical diagnosis.
Happiness was often connected with personal achievement.
Happiness was viewed as unrelated to success.
entries.promptZh: 美国大学生的回答中出现了什么联系？
optionsZh: 幸福被完全定义为继承的财富。
学生一致认为悲伤是一项医学诊断。
幸福常被联系到个人成就。
幸福被视为与成功无关。

entries.prompt: Which conditional reasoning is described as common among many people?
options: Failure always produces success before happiness.
Happiness and success are treated as unrelated concepts.
Success is possible only when a person feels unhappy.
Not being happy is taken to imply not being successful.
entries.promptZh: 本段说，许多人采用怎样的条件推理？
optionsZh: 失败总会先带来成功，再带来幸福。
幸福与成功被看作无关。
只有不幸福时才可能成功。
不幸福被理解为不成功。

entries.prompt: How is Steinberg’s magazine cover used here?
options: As experimental proof that prosperity guarantees happiness.
As an illustration of a cultural story linking happiness with success.
As evidence that the author endorses calling unhappy people losers.
As a record of who won a real happiness competition.
entries.promptZh: Steinberg 的杂志封面在这里起什么作用？
optionsZh: 作为富裕保证幸福的实验证据。
展示把幸福与成功相联的文化叙事。
证明作者赞同把不幸福者称为失败者。
记录一场真实幸福比赛的获胜者。

entries.prompt: What qualification does the passage make about happiness after a major accomplishment?
options: Its effect seems to fade within about six months.
Its effect is guaranteed to last for life.
Every accomplishment immediately reduces happiness.
Promotions affect happiness only after six months have passed.
entries.promptZh: 本段怎样限定重大成就带来的幸福？
optionsZh: 其影响似乎会在六个月内消退。
其影响保证持续一生。
每项成就都会立刻降低幸福。
晋升只有过了六个月才影响幸福。

entries.prompt: What is the affective forecasting error described in the passage?
options: Accurately predicting lasting happiness from every success.
Predicting both success-related joy and failure-related distress as greater than they turn out to be.
Underestimating the value of every possible promotion.
Expecting failure to make people happier than success.
entries.promptZh: 片段所述的情感预测偏差是什么？
optionsZh: 准确预测每次成功带来的持久幸福。
把成功的喜悦和失败的痛苦都预测得比实际更强烈。
低估每一种可能晋升的价值。
预期失败会比成功使人更幸福。

entries.prompt: How did the tenure study distinguish expectations from experienced outcomes?
options: It asked only tenured professors to predict other people’s careers.
It randomly granted tenure to every participant.
It asked current assistant professors for predictions, then interviewed people with actual tenure outcomes.
It treated the assistants’ predictions as the final measured outcomes.
entries.promptZh: 终身教职研究怎样区分预期与实际经历？
optionsZh: 只让已获终身教职者预测别人的职业。
随机给予每位参与者终身教职。
先询问现任助理教授的预测，再访谈已实际经历结果的人。
把助理教授的预测直接当成最终实际结果。

entries.prompt: What comparison does this sentence make?
options: Tenured professors were less happy than every rejected applicant.
Actual happiness after tenure was lower than current assistants had imagined.
Current assistants were unhappy because they had already lost tenure.
Receiving tenure was shown to make all recipients unhappy.
entries.promptZh: 这句话作了什么比较？
optionsZh: 获终身教职者比每位遭拒者都不幸福。
获得教职后的实际幸福低于现任助理教授的想象。
现任助理教授因已经失去教职而不幸福。
获得教职被证明让所有获得者都不幸福。

entries.prompt: How did former assistant professors who were denied tenure compare with current professors’ expectations?
options: They refused to discuss their happiness.
They were happier than the current professors had imagined.
They were guaranteed to become happier than all tenured professors.
They were exactly as devastated as predicted.
entries.promptZh: 未获终身教职的前助理教授，实际状态与现任教授的预期相比如何？
optionsZh: 他们拒绝讨论自己的幸福感。
他们比现任教授原先想象的更幸福。
他们必然比所有获得终身教职的教授更幸福。
他们恰好像预测的一样悲痛欲绝。

entries.prompt: What does the passage identify as building long-term happiness?
options: A single major victory that removes the need for daily contact.
The permanent excitement of every promotion.
Having a first child rather than maintaining friendships.
Small recurring experiences such as daily coffee with a close friend.
entries.promptZh: 本段认为什么能积累长期幸福？
optionsZh: 一次重大胜利，使日常交往不再必要。
每次晋升带来的永久兴奋。
生第一个孩子，而非维持友谊。
日常反复的小经历，例如每天和挚友喝咖啡。

entries.prompt: Which pattern is emphasised as a source of long-term happiness?
options: One sufficiently intense personal achievement.
Repeated small positive events and close relationships.
Frequent public recognition of individual success.
Avoiding every form of social interaction.
entries.promptZh: 作为长久幸福的来源，文中强调了哪种模式？
optionsZh: 一次足够强烈的个人成就。
反复出现的小型积极事件和亲密关系。
个人成功频繁获得公众认可。
避免一切形式的社会互动。

entries.prompt: What belief is conveyed by “Fake it till you make it” as explained here?
options: Continuing to act successful may eventually lead to success.
Pretending and succeeding are always unrelated.
Everyone who appears successful has already achieved every goal.
The saying advises people to abandon any appearance of success.
entries.promptZh: 本段怎样解释“Fake it till you make it”所传达的信念？
optionsZh: 持续装作成功，最终可能真正成功。
假装与成功总是无关。
看起来成功的人都已实现所有目标。
这句话建议放弃任何成功的表象。

entries.prompt: Which limitation is explicitly attributed to the first iPhone?
options: It had no stored programmes of any kind.
It could not run even a single programme.
It could not run multiple programmes at the same time.
Its memory problem occurred only when switched off.
entries.promptZh: 原文明示第一代 iPhone 有什么限制？
optionsZh: 完全没有任何已存储程序。
连一个程序也无法运行。
无法同时运行多个程序。
内存问题只在关机时发生。

entries.prompt: How did Jobs respond when a phone crashed during the launch demonstration?
options: He increased that phone’s bandwidth without switching devices.
He continued using the same phone throughout every crash.
He permanently repaired the memory before continuing.
He switched to a new iPhone during the demonstration.
entries.promptZh: 发布演示中一部手机崩溃时，Jobs 怎样应对？
optionsZh: 不更换设备，直接增加该机带宽。
每次崩溃后仍始终使用同一部手机。
先永久修好内存再继续。
在演示中换用一部新的 iPhone。

entries.prompt: What is the function of the final question beginning with “Likewise”?
options: It concludes that successful people no longer need to pretend.
It raises a possible belief by analogy with accounts of apparent success.
It reports participants’ answers to a study of American happiness.
It establishes that pretending to be happy reliably improves mood.
entries.promptZh: 以“Likewise”开头的最后一个问句起什么作用？
optionsZh: 断言成功的人不再需要假装。
通过与表面成功的故事类比，提出一种可能的信念。
报告参与者在一项美国幸福研究中的回答。
确立假装幸福能可靠地改善心情。

entries.prompt: What did participants evaluate after holding a pen in their mouth?
options: How successfully they had become popular.
How funny several cartoons were.
How often most Americans pretended to smile.
Whether their own happiness beliefs were correct.
entries.promptZh: 参与者嘴里叼笔之后，评价了什么？
optionsZh: 自己变得多受欢迎。
几幅漫画有多好笑。
多数美国人多久假笑一次。
自己的幸福观是否正确。

entries.prompt: Which result is reported for the pen experiment in this excerpt?
options: The smile group received different and objectively funnier cartoons.
The non-smile group rated the same cartoons as funnier.
The smile group rated the same cartoons as funnier than the non-smile group.
The experiment compared naturally extraverted and introverted people.
entries.promptZh: 此片段报告叼笔实验的哪个结果？
optionsZh: 微笑组看了不同且客观更好笑的漫画。
不微笑组认为同样的漫画更好笑。
微笑组比不微笑组认为同样的漫画更好笑。
实验比较天生外向者和内向者。

entries.prompt: What does the passage report about replications of the pen-in-the-mouth experiment?
options: All attempts confirmed it without exception.
Some attempts failed to replicate it, while others succeeded.
The author says replication is irrelevant to interpretation.
No researchers ever tried to repeat it.
entries.promptZh: 文中如何报告口中含笔实验的复现情况？
optionsZh: 所有尝试都毫无例外地确认了结果。
一些尝试未能复现，另一些则成功了。
作者说复现与解释无关。
从未有研究者尝试重复该实验。

entries.prompt: Which statement best preserves the reported result of the extraversion experiments?
options: Only people who were already extraverts reported greater happiness.
The studies established that fake smiling works as reliably as social interaction.
Acting more extravertedly increased reported happiness, even among natural introverts.
Talking to strangers produced the amount of happiness participants had expected.
entries.promptZh: 哪一项最准确地保留了外向行为实验所报告的结果？
optionsZh: 只有原本外向的人报告幸福感增加。
研究确立假笑与社交互动同样可靠有效。
表现得更外向增加了报告的幸福感，天性内向者也如此。
与陌生人交谈产生的幸福感恰好符合参与者预期。

entries.prompt: Which statement preserves the qualification in the passage’s conclusion?
options: Acting more extraverted tends to increase happiness, even if fake smiling does not.
Fake smiling and acting extraverted always have identical effects.
Every introvert becomes permanently happier after one social interaction.
Replicated findings show that all attempts to change behaviour fail.
entries.promptZh: 哪一说法保留了本段结论的限定？
optionsZh: 表现得更外向通常会提升幸福，即使假笑没有这种作用。
假笑与外向行为总有完全相同的效果。
每个内向者只社交一次就永久更幸福。
重复验证证明所有改变行为的尝试都会失败。

entries.prompt: How does the passage frame sadness, anger, and anxiety?
options: They invariably show that a person has failed.
They should never arise in ordinary situations.
They disappear whenever anagrams are used in experiments.
They are natural in some situations, rather than proof of failure.
entries.promptZh: 本段怎样看待悲伤、愤怒和焦虑？
optionsZh: 它们无一例外说明一个人失败了。
它们不应在日常情境中出现。
只要实验采用字母重排题，它们就会消失。
它们在某些情境下很自然，并非失败的证明。

entries.prompt: Why is the impossible-anagram experiment discussed?
options: To establish that the control group solved all the anagrams.
To recommend failure as the only route to happiness.
To prove that everyone lacks language ability.
To show that pressure to be happy can worsen reactions to the same failure.
entries.promptZh: 为什么讨论无法解开的字谜实验？
optionsZh: 证明对照组解出了全部字谜。
建议把失败作为幸福的唯一路径。
证明所有人都缺乏语言能力。
说明必须快乐的压力可能使人对同样的失败反应更糟。

entries.prompt: What changes the emotional impact of the same failure?
options: An objectively more serious failure occurs.
Believing that one is supposed to be happy makes it feel worse.
The belief that happiness is expected removes all disappointment.
The failure becomes less important when happiness is required.
entries.promptZh: 什么改变了同一次失败带来的情绪影响？
optionsZh: 失败本身客观上变得更严重。
相信自己理应快乐，会使失败感觉更糟。
认为理应幸福会消除一切失望。
要求快乐时，失败会变得更不重要。

entries.prompt: What does the international study establish in this sentence?
options: Americans felt greater average pressure to be happy than the three other named groups.
Every American felt more pressure than every Japanese participant.
Germans were happier than Americans in every measured respect.
The comparison included Americans and Japanese participants only.
entries.promptZh: 这句话中的国际研究说明了什么？
optionsZh: 美国人平均感到的快乐压力高于另外三个被列出的群体。
每个美国人的压力都高于每个日本参与者。
德国人在所有测量方面都比美国人幸福。
比较仅包括美国人和日本人。

entries.prompt: Which conclusion stays within the evidence of the international comparison?
options: Every American feels more pressure than every Japanese person.
Countries associating happiness more with luck appeared to show less pressure to be happy.
Cultural associations were experimentally assigned to entire nations.
Belief in luck has been proved to remove all sadness.
entries.promptZh: 哪一项结论没有超出跨国比较的证据范围？
optionsZh: 每个美国人承受的压力都比每个日本人大。
将幸福更多联系到运气的国家，似乎显示出较小的快乐压力。
各个国家的文化联系是实验随机分配的。
相信运气已被证实可以消除所有悲伤。

entries.prompt: What additional pressure was associated with pressure to feel happy?
options: Pressure to feel sad and angry more frequently.
Pressure to avoid all social relationships.
Pressure not to experience sadness and anger.
Pressure to report happiness only in research settings.
entries.promptZh: 感到必须幸福的人，还伴随着什么压力？
optionsZh: 更频繁地感到悲伤和愤怒的压力。
回避所有社会关系的压力。
不应体验悲伤和愤怒的压力。
只在研究场景中报告幸福的压力。

entries.prompt: In this sentence, “faces” most nearly means which of the following?
options: Stages.
Aspects.
Expressions.
Outcomes.
entries.promptZh: 这句话中的“faces”最接近哪个意思？
optionsZh: 阶段。
方面。
表情。
结果。

entries.prompt: Why does the author place “And yet” before the statement about negative emotions?
options: To show that unavoidable feelings conflict with the demand to be happy.
To deny that pressure changes how people view sadness.
To explain that criticism is less upsetting than missing a train.
To introduce the second face of the happiness trap in full.
entries.promptZh: 作者为什么在负面情绪的陈述前使用“And yet”？
optionsZh: 说明不可避免的感受与必须快乐的要求之间存在冲突。
否认压力会改变人们看待悲伤的方式。
解释受到批评比错过火车更不令人难受。
完整介绍幸福陷阱的第二面。

entries.prompt: How does the author characterise feeling bad after the listed events?
options: As proof that the person has failed at life.
As evidence that criticism is always justified.
As a feeling limited to parents and train passengers.
As a natural response to unpleasant experiences.
entries.promptZh: 作者怎样看待列举事件后产生的难受？
optionsZh: 证明这个人的人生失败了。
证明批评总是合理的。
这种感受只限于父母和火车乘客。
这是对不愉快经历的自然反应。

entries.prompt: What did the young woman do that prompted the author to thank her?
options: She brought him food from the Chinese restaurant.
She arranged for a door attendant to assist him.
She opened the building door for him.
She carried his meal upstairs to his flat.
entries.promptZh: 那位年轻女子做了什么，使作者向她道谢？
optionsZh: 从中餐馆给他带来食物。
安排门房协助他。
为他打开楼门。
把他的饭菜送上楼。

entries.prompt: In the doorway anecdote, “completely thrown off” most nearly means that the author was:
options: physically prevented from entering his building.
confused by an unexpected response.
pleased to be recognised by a neighbour.
uncertain whether he had ordered the correct food.
entries.promptZh: 在门口的轶事中，“completely thrown off”最接近下列哪种意思？
optionsZh: 身体上被阻止进入自己的大楼。
被出乎意料的回应弄得困惑。
因为被邻居认出来而感到高兴。
不确定自己是否点了正确的食物。

entries.prompt: At which stages of his career did the author say these experiences occurred?
options: Both as a graduate student and as a full professor.
Only before he began graduate school.
As a graduate student, but never as a professor.
Only after he retired from academic work.
entries.promptZh: 作者说，这些经历发生在职业生涯的哪些阶段？
optionsZh: 研究生时期和正教授时期都有。
仅在开始研究生学习之前。
研究生时期有，成为教授后从未有。
仅在退出学术工作之后。

entries.prompt: What was the context of Kahneman’s inquiry about the author?
options: The author was applying to begin undergraduate study at Princeton.
Diener had applied to become a student of the author.
The author had already accepted a full professorship at Princeton.
The author had applied for an assistant professor position at Princeton.
entries.promptZh: Kahneman 打听作者的情况，背景是什么？
optionsZh: 作者正在申请普林斯顿的本科。
Diener 申请成为作者的学生。
作者已经接受普林斯顿的正教授职位。
作者申请了普林斯顿的助理教授职位。

entries.prompt: How did the advisor respond after Kahneman said survival at Princeton required being cocky?
options: He changed his description and called the author cocky.
He mentioned another student of his who was cocky.
He denied that Kahneman had made such a requirement.
He described Kahneman as his own cockiest student.
entries.promptZh: Kahneman 说在普林斯顿生存需要自负之后，导师怎样回应？
optionsZh: 改口说作者自负。
提到自己另一个自负的学生。
否认 Kahneman 提出过这一要求。
把 Kahneman 称为自己最自负的学生。

entries.prompt: What outcome does the author explicitly report one week after the conversation?
options: His lab mate received an interview that he himself did not receive.
Kahneman interviewed him but rejected him after the meeting.
His lab mate accepted the Princeton job instead of him.
His advisor withdrew his application before Princeton considered it.
entries.promptZh: 作者明确报告，谈话一周后发生了什么？
optionsZh: 同门获得了面试机会，而作者自己没有。
卡尼曼面试了作者，却在面谈后拒绝了他。
同门代替作者接受了普林斯顿的职位。
导师在普林斯顿考虑之前撤回了作者的申请。

entries.prompt: Which statement best preserves “not always fair”?
options: Every event in the world is fair.
No event in the world is ever fair.
Some events can be unfair.
Fairness can be assumed in every situation.
entries.promptZh: 哪项改写最准确保留“not always fair”的意思？
optionsZh: 世界上的每件事都公平。
世界上从来没有任何公平的事。
有些事情可能不公平。
任何情境都可以假定公平。

entries.prompt: What does the final question invite the reader to consider?
options: How people respond when they feel bad.
Why unfair events can never produce bad feelings.
Which country has the highest average income.
The measured success rate of one named therapy.
entries.promptZh: 最后的问句邀请读者思考什么？
optionsZh: 人在难受时怎样应对。
为什么不公平事件绝不产生难受感。
哪个国家平均收入最高。
某项具名疗法测得的成功率。

entries.prompt: How does the passage classify attempts to repair mood?
options: Exercise and hiking are described as unhealthy attempts.
Over-drinking and impulsive shopping are the healthy examples.
Everyone under pressure chooses an identical method.
People may use healthy or unhealthy methods to improve mood.
entries.promptZh: 本段怎样区分修复心情的尝试？
optionsZh: 锻炼和徒步被说成不健康的尝试。
过量饮酒和冲动购物是健康例子。
每个承受压力的人都选择同样的方法。
人们可能采用健康或不健康的方法改善心情。

entries.prompt: How should the description of “soma” be read in this passage?
options: As the author’s prescribed method for recovering from a low mood.
As a result showing that every mood-repair method is unhealthy.
As evidence from a clinical comparison of pills and exercise.
As a fictional illustration within a discussion of responses to low mood.
entries.promptZh: 应该如何理解本段对 soma 的描述？
optionsZh: 作者为摆脱低落心情开出的处方。
说明每种心情修复方法都不健康的结果。
药丸与锻炼的临床比较证据。
讨论低落心情应对方式时插入的虚构作品例子。

entries.prompt: What does the author say he does if his wife is not around?
options: He waits for her return before doing anything.
He takes a nap.
He phones her to discuss every song.
He goes shopping instead of resting.
entries.promptZh: 作者说，妻子不在身边时他会做什么？
optionsZh: 等她回来之后才采取任何行动。
小睡一会儿。
打电话和她讨论每首歌。
去购物而不是休息。

entries.prompt: What does this excerpt introduce?
options: Categories of methods for addressing a persistent negative mood.
A claim that every negative mood lasts permanently.
The abandonment of research on emotion regulation.
One method guaranteed to work for every person.
entries.promptZh: 这个片段引出了什么？
optionsZh: 处理持续负面心情的方法类别。
每种负面心情都永久持续的断言。
放弃情绪调节研究。
一个保证对每个人都有效的方法。

entries.prompt: What do the approaches in the paragraph mainly have in common?
options: They require the other person to agree to reverse the event.
They remove the original event from the person’s memory.
They change the perspective through which an upsetting event is viewed.
They treat future distress as certain to be worse than present distress.
entries.promptZh: 本段的几种方法主要有什么共同点？
optionsZh: 要求对方同意撤销已经发生的事件。
从当事人的记忆中删除原来的事件。
改变看待令人难受事件的视角。
认定未来的痛苦必然比现在更严重。

entries.prompt: What does “a tiny bump in the road” suggest about a possible future view of the event?
options: It will certainly feel just as painful forever.
It must literally have involved a road accident.
It might later seem like a minor obstacle.
Its importance will definitely increase over five years.
entries.promptZh: “道路上的一个小颠簸”暗示未来可能怎样看待这个事件？
optionsZh: 它一定永远同样痛苦。
事件字面上一定是交通事故。
以后它可能显得只是一个小障碍。
它的重要性在五年里必定增加。

entries.prompt: What attitude is attributed to people who feel less pressure to be happy?
options: They believe negative moods never occur naturally.
They reject the possibility that time can help.
They insist on removing every bad feeling immediately.
They accept occasional bad feelings and do less to repair them.
entries.promptZh: 本段描述，较少感到快乐压力的人持怎样的态度？
optionsZh: 认为负面心情绝不会自然发生。
拒绝时间可能有所帮助。
坚持立刻消除每一种难受。
接受偶尔难受，因此较少主动修复心情。

entries.prompt: What does the “psychological immune system” analogy highlight?
options: That biological viruses directly cause all unhappiness.
That negative moods should never be discussed.
That active coping methods are always ineffective.
That people have a natural capacity to recover from negative emotional states.
entries.promptZh: “心理免疫系统”的类比强调什么？
optionsZh: 生物病毒直接造成所有不幸福。
负面心情绝不应该被讨论。
主动应对方式总是无效。
人们拥有从负面情绪状态中自然恢复的能力。

entries.prompt: How is the psychological immune system described in the analogy?
options: As a biological virus produced by an unhappy thought.
As a system that activates automatically after an undesirable event.
As a deliberate technique requiring conscious practice every time.
As a system that prevents every undesirable event from happening.
entries.promptZh: 这个类比怎样描述心理免疫系统？
optionsZh: 由不快乐想法产生的生物病毒。
不如意事件发生后自动启动的系统。
每次都需要有意识练习的刻意技巧。
阻止一切不如意事件发生的系统。

entries.prompt: Which sequence of ideas best matches the author’s argument?
options: Mood-repair habits strengthen the immune system, which creates pressure to be happy.
Emotional acceptance removes every need for active emotion regulation.
Natural recovery is underestimated, while pressure can encourage reliance on unhealthy coping.
All negative moods result from shopping, so shopping must stop before recovery.
entries.promptZh: 哪一种思路最符合作者的论证？
optionsZh: 心情修复习惯增强免疫系统，由此产生必须快乐的压力。
情绪接纳消除了一切主动情绪调节的需要。
自然恢复能力被低估，而快乐压力可能使人依赖不健康的应对。
所有负面心情都源于购物，因此恢复前必须停止购物。

entries.prompt: What distinguishes a “satisficer” as defined in this passage?
options: Accepting any option regardless of whether it meets basic needs.
Refusing to make a choice until every alternative disappears.
Accepting a satisfactory option instead of insisting on the best.
Always choosing the option with the lowest objective quality.
entries.promptZh: 按本段定义，“satisficer”的特点是什么？
optionsZh: 不管是否满足基本需要，都接受任何选项。
直到所有其他选项消失才肯选择。
接受令人满意的选项，而不坚持最优。
总选择客观质量最低的选项。

entries.prompt: What decision is introduced in this hypothetical scenario?
options: Which college to choose.
Which high school to enter.
Which extracurricular activity to begin.
Which college course will provide the highest salary.
entries.promptZh: 这个假设情境提出了什么决定？
optionsZh: 选择哪所大学。
进入哪所高中。
开始哪项课外活动。
哪门大学课程将带来最高薪水。

entries.prompt: Why is the person in this example called a maximizer?
options: Applying to ten schools is presented as the sole universal test.
The person prefers any acceptable option over the best possible one.
The person has already been rejected by ten colleges.
The person seeks the best possible college and applies to ten schools.
entries.promptZh: 例子中的人为什么被称为最大化选择者？
optionsZh: 申请十所学校被当作唯一且普遍的判定标准。
比起最好选择，此人更偏爱任何可接受选项。
此人已经被十所大学拒绝。
此人追求可能进入的最好大学，并申请十所学校。

entries.prompt: What distinguishes the satisficer in the college-choice example?
options: The student chooses a satisfactory option that meets stated needs.
The student lacks the grades required to consider elite universities.
The student treats the highest possible prestige as the only requirement.
The student applies to every school before choosing the cheapest offer.
entries.promptZh: 择校例子中，满足者的特点是什么？
optionsZh: 选择一个达到自身明确要求、令人满意的选项。
没有足够成绩去考虑顶尖大学。
把尽可能高的声望当作唯一要求。
申请每一所学校后再选择最便宜的录取。

entries.prompt: What outcome is reported for the study featuring the college-choice scenario?
options: The Cornell maximizer was necessarily happier because of the school’s prestige.
The UVA satisficer was likely happier than the Cornell maximizer.
Every UVA student was happier than every Cornell student.
Decision style was absent from the comparison.
entries.promptZh: 包含择校情境的研究报告了什么结果？
optionsZh: 康奈尔的最大化选择者因学校声望而必然更幸福。
弗吉尼亚大学的满意即可者可能比康奈尔的最大化选择者更幸福。
每位弗吉尼亚大学学生都比每位康奈尔学生幸福。
比较中没有涉及决策心态。

entries.prompt: What explains the UVA–Cornell example in the passage?
options: A controlled demonstration that tuition alone determines happiness.
Evidence that every Cornell student regrets enrolling.
The number of imagined alternative outcomes, rather than a claim that one university is inherently better.
A rule that all students should apply to ten schools.
entries.promptZh: 文中的 UVA 与康奈尔大学例子，核心解释是什么？
optionsZh: 一项证明只有学费决定幸福的受控实验。
每个康奈尔学生都后悔入学的证据。
想象的备选结局数量，而非某所大学本来就更优越。
所有学生都应申请十所学校的规则。

entries.prompt: How do the two “If I...” statements function here?
options: They imagine alternative past conditions, contrasted with the satisficer’s lack of counterfactuals.
They report Yale and Princeton offers that were actually received.
They show that the UVA satisficer applied to more schools than anyone else.
They establish that no alternatives could ever be imagined.
entries.promptZh: 两句“If I...”在这里起什么作用？
optionsZh: 设想不同的过去条件，与满意即可者没有反事实想法形成对照。
报告实际收到的耶鲁和普林斯顿录取。
说明弗吉尼亚大学的满意即可者比所有人申请得更多。
证明永远不可能想象其他选择。

entries.prompt: Which approach does the author recommend in this passage?
options: Keep dwelling on rejection from the preferred school.
Avoid noticing positive features of the current school.
Adopt a good-enough mindset and notice what is good about the current school.
Treat entry to an elite school as a guarantee of happiness.
entries.promptZh: 本段中，作者推荐哪种做法？
optionsZh: 持续想着被最想去的学校拒绝。
避免注意现在学校的优点。
采取足够好的心态，并发现当前学校的好处。
把进入名校当作幸福保证。

entries.prompt: How does the opening sentence connect upward social comparison with the discussion?
options: It says maximizing always protects people from comparing themselves with others.
It presents entrepreneurial success as making upward comparison impossible.
It treats Clark’s career as a series of business failures.
It links upward comparison to maximizing and calls it another source of unhappiness.
entries.promptZh: 首句怎样把向上社会比较接入讨论？
optionsZh: 说最大化心态总能保护人不与别人比较。
把创业成功说成能使向上比较不可能发生。
把 Clark 的职业经历说成一连串商业失败。
将向上比较与最大化心态相联，称其为不幸福的另一个来源。

entries.prompt: What does Jim Clark’s sequence of wealth targets chiefly illustrate?
options: Comparing fortunes proves that wealth is unrelated to any life outcome.
Financial success guarantees satisfaction once a fixed target is reached.
Every successful entrepreneur measures happiness in exactly the same way.
Repeated success need not end dissatisfaction when comparison targets keep moving.
entries.promptZh: 吉姆·克拉克不断变化的财富目标主要说明什么？
optionsZh: 比较财富证明财富与任何人生结果都无关。
达到一个固定目标后，财务成功就保证满足感。
每个成功企业家都以完全相同的方式衡量幸福。
比较目标不断移动时，反复成功也未必能终结不满足。

entries.prompt: Which claim is presented as a research finding rather than speculation about Clark?
options: Clark’s personal satisfaction was directly measured and confirmed.
People avoiding upward comparison were happier than those obsessed with comparison.
Clark was reported to be wealthier than Ellison in 2023.
Lyubomirsky and Ross studied only Clark and Ellison.
entries.promptZh: 哪项被作为研究发现提出，而非对 Clark 的猜测？
optionsZh: Clark 的个人满足感被直接测量并确认。
不做向上比较的人，比执着比较的人更幸福。
据报道，2023 年 Clark 比 Ellison 更富有。
Lyubomirsky 和 Ross 只研究了 Clark 与 Ellison。

entries.prompt: What position does the passage take on avoiding upward comparison on social media?
options: It is difficult but possible.
It is impossible without any exception.
It is unnecessary because online images show everyone’s complete life.
It is easy because the images are randomly selected.
entries.promptZh: 本段怎样看待在社交媒体上避免向上比较？
optionsZh: 困难，但可能做到。
绝无例外地不可能。
不必要，因为网上图像展示每个人的完整生活。
容易，因为这些图像随机选取。

entries.prompt: In what capacity does the narrator introduce Mr. Johnson?
options: A university admissions officer addressing applicants.
The narrator’s former professor at UVA.
A middle-school principal telling parents and students about his college years.
A journalist interviewing parents about school rankings.
entries.promptZh: 叙述者以什么身份介绍 Johnson 先生？
optionsZh: 向申请者讲话的大学招生官。
叙述者在弗吉尼亚大学的前教授。
向家长和学生讲述大学往事的中学校长。
采访家长、讨论学校排名的记者。

entries.prompt: Why does the author recall the story about trash bags and suitcases?
options: To suggest that matching others’ possessions resolves social comparison.
To establish that suitcases cause students to feel inferior.
To prove that carefully curated images reveal complete lives.
To show that social comparisons can be resisted by accepting difference.
entries.promptZh: 作者为什么回忆垃圾袋与行李箱的故事？
optionsZh: 暗示拥有与他人相同的物品就能解决社会比较。
确立行李箱会使学生自卑。
证明精心挑选的图像展示了完整的人生。
说明可以通过接纳差异来抵抗社会比较。

entries.prompt: Why did the BBC seek the key to happiness among Danes, according to this excerpt?
options: Denmark often ranks among the world’s happiest countries.
Denmark was said to have no unhappy residents.
The BBC had already proved that national wealth alone creates happiness.
The Danes had asked the BBC to change a university ranking.
entries.promptZh: 根据片段，BBC 为什么向丹麦人寻找幸福秘诀？
optionsZh: 丹麦经常位列世界最幸福国家之一。
据称丹麦没有不快乐的居民。
BBC 已证明只有国家财富创造幸福。
丹麦人要求 BBC 改大学排名。

entries.prompt: How does the passage explain “hygge”?
options: Comfort and modest everyday pleasures associated with contentment.
Competitive ambition directed at Denmark’s national ranking.
The BBC’s method for calculating international happiness scores.
A rule requiring everyone to avoid long-term expectations.
entries.promptZh: 片段怎样解释 hygge？
optionsZh: 与知足相联系的舒适感和日常小乐趣。
针对丹麦国家排名的竞争抱负。
BBC 计算国际幸福分数的方法。
要求所有人避免长期期待的一条规则。

entries.prompt: What stance does the author take toward the satisficer mindset here?
options: It should replace maximizing in every area of life.
It has no legitimate use in ordinary decisions.
It is useful only when a person stops planning.
It has an important place, without being universally preferred to maximizing.
entries.promptZh: 作者在这里对满意即可心态持什么立场？
optionsZh: 应在生活所有方面取代最大化心态。
在日常决定中没有合理用途。
只有停止规划时才有用。
它有重要作用，但不因此应一概优先于最大化心态。

entries.prompt: What limitation of the satisficer mindset does the author identify?
options: Contentment with the status quo can discourage necessary challenges and growth.
It necessarily makes all people financially poorer.
It always creates more counterfactuals than maximising.
It can never be useful in everyday decisions.
entries.promptZh: 作者指出满足者心态有什么局限？
optionsZh: 满足现状可能使人不愿迎接必要挑战和个人成长。
它必然使所有人在财务上更贫穷。
它总会比最大化追求产生更多反事实设想。
它在日常决策中从来没有用处。

entries.prompt: How does the quotation from John support the warning?
options: It experimentally proves that unhappiness always improves health.
It voices rejection of a false happiness that can accompany settling for less.
It declares that all satisfaction is necessarily dishonest.
It shows that John recommends avoiding every challenge.
entries.promptZh: John 的引述怎样支持这里的警示？
optionsZh: 用实验证明不幸福总能改善健康。
表达对满足于较少所得时可能伴随的虚假幸福的拒绝。
宣称所有满足感必然不诚实。
说明 John 建议逃避一切挑战。

entries.prompt: Whose view is associated with people being deceived into happiness and virtue?
options: The BBC’s conclusion from a controlled trial.
The author’s claim about every survey respondent.
Nietzsche’s view, introduced through his writing.
A clinical diagnosis offered by John.
entries.promptZh: “人们被诱骗而幸福且有德”被归为谁的观点？
optionsZh: BBC 的对照试验结论。
作者对每位调查受访者的断言。
通过其著作引入的 Nietzsche 的观点。
John 给出的临床诊断。

entries.prompt: What criticism does the quoted speaker make about seeking contentment?
options: It invariably produces the greatest possible virtue.
It prevents all forms of resignation.
It is presented as a scientific measure of physical size.
It can shrink aspiration into modest virtue and repeated small happinesses.
entries.promptZh: 引述中的说话者怎样批评对满足的追求？
optionsZh: 它必然产生最大美德。
它能防止任何认命。
它是测量身体尺寸的科学方法。
它会让追求缩小为有限的美德和接连的小幸福。

entries.prompt: In the quoted passage, why is pleasing everybody criticised?
options: It prevents anyone from enjoying even a small amount of contentment.
It demonstrates that the speakers have attained the highest possible virtue.
It is portrayed as an attempt to avoid being hurt, even when called virtue.
It is shown by an experiment to reduce all forms of happiness.
entries.promptZh: 在所引片段中，为什么批评取悦所有人？
optionsZh: 它使说话者连一丝知足也无法享有。
它显示说话者已经达到最高的美德。
它被描写成避免受伤的企图，即使被称作美德。
实验显示它会减少所有形式的幸福。

entries.prompt: What kind of life does Nietzsche advocate in this excerpt?
options: A wandering life that embraces difficult heights and depths.
A comfortable life protected from every uncertainty.
A settled life based exclusively on public approval.
A life in which greatness removes all danger.
entries.promptZh: Nietzsche 在这段中提倡怎样的生活？
optionsZh: 漂泊探索、迎向艰难高峰与深渊的生活。
受到保护、不存在任何不确定性的舒适生活。
完全建立在公众认可之上的安定生活。
达到伟大便消除一切危险的生活。

entries.prompt: Which statement best restates the reversal described in the quotation?
options: The traveller abandons greatness to avoid danger.
All faraway places are guaranteed to be safe.
What was once the greatest danger becomes the greatest refuge.
Refuge is available only to people who remain at home.
entries.promptZh: 哪一项最准确地改写了引述中的转变？
optionsZh: 旅行者放弃伟大以躲避危险。
所有遥远地方都保证安全。
曾经最大的危险成了最大的庇护。
只有留在家里的人才能获得庇护。

entries.prompt: To whom does the quoted speaker address his riddle?
options: Readers who insist that every answer be supplied in advance.
Bold searchers willing to venture into uncertainty.
Officials responsible for guaranteeing safe sea travel.
People who reject every form of exploration.
entries.promptZh: 引述中的说话者把谜题讲给谁？
optionsZh: 坚持所有答案必须预先给出的读者。
愿意冒险进入未知的勇敢探索者。
负责保证海上交通安全的官员。
拒绝一切探索的人。

entries.prompt: Why are “small happiness and meaning” described as dangerous here?
options: They can attract people into a conventional life that avoids conflict.
They make people consciously choose the greatest physical danger.
They require everyone to become literal mountain climbers.
They are rejected because a comfortable life cannot contain any meaning.
entries.promptZh: 这里为什么把“小小的幸福与意义”描述为危险的？
optionsZh: 它们可能吸引人进入避免冲突的惯常生活。
它们使人有意识地选择最大的身体危险。
它们要求所有人真正成为登山者。
它们遭到否定，因为舒适生活不可能包含任何意义。

entries.prompt: What can be established from this sentence alone?
options: Every person agreed with Zarathustra’s judgement.
The sentence supplies experimental evidence about happiness.
Zarathustra regarded every possible life as worthless.
Zarathustra judged the life under discussion not worth living.
entries.promptZh: 仅凭这句话，能确定什么？
optionsZh: 所有人都同意查拉图斯特拉的判断。
这句话提供了幸福实验的证据。
查拉图斯特拉认为所有可能的生活都无价值。
查拉图斯特拉认为当时讨论的那种生活不值得过。

entries.prompt: Which statement best captures the balance of the chapter’s closing advice?
options: Negative feelings should replace happiness as the only aim of life.
Only people who are currently unhappy can live a good life.
A happy person should abandon all sources of comfort and small joy.
Accept occasional negative feelings and consider possibilities beyond contentment.
entries.promptZh: 哪一项最能概括章末建议所保持的平衡？
optionsZh: 负面感受应当取代幸福，成为人生的唯一目标。
只有目前不幸福的人才能过上美好生活。
幸福的人应当放弃所有舒适与小乐趣。
接纳偶尔的负面感受，并考虑知足之外的更多可能。

entries.prompt: What do the quotations from Flaubert and Schwartz illustrate?
options: Happiness has critics who associate it with unattractive qualities.
Medical studies have established stupidity as necessary for happiness.
Everyone writing about happiness agrees that it is desirable.
The Stoics conducted the research cited by Schwartz.
entries.promptZh: Flaubert 和 Schwartz 的引述说明什么？
optionsZh: 幸福也有批评者，他们把它与并不讨喜的特征联系起来。
医学研究已确认愚蠢是幸福的必要条件。
所有谈幸福的作者都认为幸福值得追求。
斯多葛学派开展了 Schwartz 引用的研究。

entries.prompt: How does Silverstein’s closing remark function in this account of his poem?
options: It reports a measured decline in a country’s happiness.
It shows that no one in the imagined land is happy.
It punctures the appeal of a place where everything is happy and jolly.
It recommends that readers move to the land described.
entries.promptZh: 这段介绍中，Silverstein 的结尾评论起什么作用？
optionsZh: 报告某国幸福度经测量下降。
表明想象中的地方没有一个人幸福。
削弱了那个人人幸福、处处欢乐之地的吸引力。
建议读者搬去所描写的地方。

entries.prompt: How does the spending example relate to the critique of happiness?
options: It confirms that happiness requires selfish spending.
It provides a counterexample to the claim that a happy life must be selfish.
It shows that spending on oneself and others has identical effects.
It establishes that money is the only source of happiness.
entries.promptZh: 花钱的例子与对幸福的批评是什么关系？
optionsZh: 证实幸福必须靠自私消费。
反驳幸福生活必定自私这一说法。
表明为自己和别人花钱的效果完全相同。
确认金钱是幸福的唯一来源。

entries.prompt: Why does the author temporarily assume the happiness-as-selfishness critique?
options: To withdraw the statement that happy people volunteer more.
To claim that volunteering makes everyone unhappy.
To prove that happiness never contributes to a good life.
To explore what could make a life good apart from happiness.
entries.promptZh: 作者为什么暂时接受“幸福即自私”的批评作假定？
optionsZh: 撤回幸福的人志愿服务更多的说法。
断言志愿服务让所有人不幸福。
证明幸福从不有助于美好生活。
探索幸福之外还有什么能使生活美好。

entries.prompt: How is significance first explained in this account of meaning in life?
options: A life matters to people beyond one’s family and friends.
A person receives public awards for every achievement.
A life has no obligations to strangers.
A person feels happy at every other person’s expense.
entries.promptZh: 这里首先怎样解释生命意义中的重要性？
optionsZh: 一个人的生活对家人朋友之外的人也有分量。
一个人每项成就都获得公众奖项。
一个人的生活对陌生人没有责任。
一个人靠牺牲所有他人的利益来幸福。

entries.prompt: What does knowing where one is going mean in this passage?
options: Remembering the route to every place one has visited.
Avoiding all changes in a daily timetable.
Having a clear purpose and a guiding sense of direction.
Making a difference only within one’s immediate family.
entries.promptZh: 片段中“知道自己往哪里走”是什么意思？
optionsZh: 记得去过的每个地方的路线。
避免日程发生任何变化。
有明确目的和引导自己的方向感。
只对自己的直系亲属产生影响。

entries.prompt: What makes the experiences described here form a meaningful whole?
options: They are identical in every respect.
They fit together under the person’s guiding principles.
They are kept separate from any personal principles.
They occur in a strictly unchanging order.
entries.promptZh: 这里的经历怎样构成一个有意义的整体？
optionsZh: 每项经历在所有方面都相同。
在这个人自己的指导原则下彼此契合。
与任何个人原则保持分离。
按严格不变的顺序发生。

entries.prompt: What distinguishes a “bullshit job” in Graeber’s definition here?
options: It requires strenuous physical labour.
It is any occupation held by millions of people.
It offers no opportunity to change employers.
Its holder cannot really justify why the job exists.
entries.promptZh: 在 Graeber 这里的定义中，“bullshit job”的区别性特征是什么？
optionsZh: 需要繁重体力劳动。
任何有数百万人从事的职业。
没有换雇主的机会。
从业者自己无法真正说明这份工作存在的理由。

entries.prompt: Why does the author say these occupations do not necessarily imply meaningless lives?
options: People can make a difference outside their jobs.
Graeber excludes all professional occupations from his argument.
The author claims that every corporate lawyer secretly enjoys the work.
A job’s repetitiveness guarantees a meaningful life.
entries.promptZh: 作者为什么说这些职业并不必然意味着无意义的人生？
optionsZh: 人们也能在工作之外产生影响。
Graeber 将所有专业职业排除在论证之外。
作者断言每位公司律师都暗中喜欢这份工作。
工作的重复性保证人生有意义。

entries.prompt: Which combination characterises the meaningless life described here?
options: Public recognition, a fixed destination, and emotional calm.
An ambitious career combined with frequent changes of employer.
A lack of positive impact, clear purpose, and a sense of wholeness.
Low income despite a strong sense of purpose.
entries.promptZh: 哪组特征概括这里描述的无意义生活？
optionsZh: 公众认可、固定目的地与情绪平静。
有野心的事业与频繁换雇主。
缺少正面影响、明确目的和整体感。
虽很有目的感但收入低。

entries.prompt: What does the sentence say about the roles a person plays?
options: They are too numerous for anyone to remember.
They fail to come together as an integrated whole.
They are necessarily limited to paid employment.
They all express one clearly unified purpose.
entries.promptZh: 这句话对一个人承担的不同角色作了什么描述？
optionsZh: 角色太多，任何人都记不住。
它们无法相互整合为连贯整体。
它们必然只限于有报酬的工作。
它们都表达一个明确统一的目的。

entries.prompt: Which statement accurately reflects the routes to a reason for living listed here?
options: A career is presented as the only acceptable route.
Social change is excluded because it involves others.
All people must make a scientific discovery before life can have meaning.
Several routes are offered, including career, religion, and social roles.
entries.promptZh: 哪一项准确反映这里列举的人生理由的来源？
optionsZh: 事业是唯一可接受的途径。
社会变革因涉及他人而被排除。
所有人必须先有科学发现，人生才能有意义。
列出多条途径，包括事业、宗教和社会角色。

entries.prompt: What action is explicitly requested in this sentence?
options: Contribute to helping other people do the same.
Wait until other people have helped you first.
Take sole responsibility for every other person’s future.
Avoid helping others because success is entirely individual.
entries.promptZh: 这句话明确要求采取什么行动？
optionsZh: 尽自己的一份力量帮助别人也做到同样的事。
先等其他人帮助自己。
独自承担所有其他人未来的全部责任。
因为成功完全是个人的事，所以不帮助别人。

entries.prompt: What event led Donna Adams-Pickett to decide to become an ob-gyn doctor?
options: Her father’s graduation from medical school.
A tobacco farm’s decision to close.
Learning that her grandmother and the baby had died during childbirth.
Hearing that her grandmother had become a doctor.
entries.promptZh: 什么事件促使 Donna Adams-Pickett 决定成为妇产科医生？
optionsZh: 父亲从医学院毕业。
一家烟草农场决定关门。
得知祖母与婴儿都在分娩时去世。
听说祖母成为医生。

entries.prompt: How does the author illustrate significance in Dr. Adams-Pickett’s life?
options: By saying that maternal care was already equally available everywhere.
By noting that some mothers and babies might have died without her care.
By proving that she personally eliminated every maternal death in Georgia.
By treating the number of television appearances as the measure of meaning.
entries.promptZh: 作者怎样说明 Adams-Pickett 医生人生的重要性？
optionsZh: 说明孕产照护早已在各地同样普及。
指出没有她的照护，一些母亲与婴儿可能已经死亡。
证明她亲自消除了佐治亚州每一例产妇死亡。
把电视出镜次数作为人生意义的衡量标准。

entries.prompt: What does “coherence” refer to in this sentence?
options: Proof that every event in her life was planned in advance.
A guarantee that family tragedy always improves a career.
The absence of any changes in the course of her life.
A convincing connection running through the story of her life.
entries.promptZh: 这句话里的 coherence 指什么？
optionsZh: 证明她所有人生事件都预先计划好了。
保证家族悲剧总能改善事业。
人生过程中从来没有任何变化。
贯穿她人生故事、令人信服的联系。

entries.prompt: What limitation does “However” introduce after the description of heroes?
options: Their extraordinary accomplishments are too rare to feel readily attainable.
The named people never achieved anything important.
Graduation speeches prevent people from having meaningful lives.
Their achievements are common enough for everyone to reproduce easily.
entries.promptZh: 描述英雄人物后，However 引入什么限制？
optionsZh: 那些非凡成就过于罕见，令人难以想象自己也能达到。
列举的人物从未成就重要的事。
毕业典礼演讲阻止人们过有意义的生活。
这些成就十分普遍，人人都容易复制。

entries.prompt: What is the first element of the meaning trap?
options: Meaningful lives necessarily require unhappiness.
People always choose goals that are too easy.
The accomplishment imagined is so grand that pursuing it sets people up for failure.
Failure proves that every part of a person’s life lacks meaning.
entries.promptZh: 意义陷阱的第一个因素是什么？
optionsZh: 有意义的生活必然需要不幸福。
人们总是选择太容易的目标。
想象中与有意义生活相联的成就过于宏大，追求它会让人陷入失败。
失败证明一个人人生的每个部分都无意义。

entries.prompt: What contrast does the author draw between popular belief and survey findings?
options: Most people reject meaning, while researchers say only heroes have it.
People imagine meaningful lives to be rare, but most respondents say their lives have meaning.
Survey data show that nearly everyone has achieved a heroic ambition.
Both popular belief and surveys say meaningful lives are limited to a tiny minority.
entries.promptZh: 作者把大众想法与调查结果作了什么对比？
optionsZh: 多数人拒绝意义，而研究者说只有英雄才有意义。
人们想象有意义的生活很少见，但多数受访者说自己的人生有意义。
调查表明几乎人人都达成英雄式抱负。
大众与调查都说只有极少数人的生活有意义。

entries.prompt: What does the reported 90 percent represent?
options: Americans who had received a national award.
All people worldwide who were independently certified as having meaningful lives.
