entries.prompt: In the explore-exploit terminology, how is the first group characterized?
options: They exploit before doing any exploration at all.
They search for fewer people over less time than the second group.
They are experimentally assigned to divorce quickly.
They explore for longer before committing to a choice.
entries.promptZh: 按探索利用术语，第一组有什么特征？
optionsZh: 完全没探索就先利用。
比第二组花更少时间接触更少人。
被随机分配迅速离婚。
投入选择前先探索较久。

entries.prompt: Why does the passage argue for more exploration in the real mating context?
options: Many potential partners differ only slightly, unlike a case with one obviously superior choice.
One partner is assumed to be overwhelmingly better in every real situation.
Computer simulations are said to prove all marriages have identical outcomes.
Exploration is claimed to have no cost under any circumstances.
entries.promptZh: 为什么片段主张现实择偶中多探索？
optionsZh: 许多潜在对象差别较小，不像一个选项明显最优的情形。
假设每个真实情境都有一人压倒性更好。
模拟证明所有婚姻结果一致。
探索在任何情况下都无成本。

entries.prompt: Which conclusion is supported by the CDC data as described?
options: Longer exploration guarantees that a marriage will last.
Shorter exploration is associated with a greater likelihood of divorce.
Divorce causes couples to shorten their premarital exploration.
Every long exploration ends in marriage.
entries.promptZh: 按片段描述，CDC 数据支持哪项结论？
optionsZh: 探索久保证婚姻持续。
探索较短与更高离婚可能性相关。
离婚导致婚前探索缩短。
每次长期探索都以婚姻告终。

entries.prompt: Why do Todd and Miller question the 37 percent rule here?
options: CDC data directly contradict all search models.
Animals can always identify the single best mate.
Finding a top-tier mate may matter more than identifying the single best one.
The rule requires animals to choose the worst available mate.
entries.promptZh: Todd 和 Miller 在这里为何质疑 37% 规则？
optionsZh: CDC 数据直接反驳全部搜索模型。
动物总能辨认唯一最优配偶。
找到优质对象可能比认出唯一最优者更重要。
规则要求动物选最差对象。

entries.prompt: Under what condition does examining the first 14 percent yield the highest success probability?
options: There are 100 potential mates and success means finding one of the best options.
There are 1,000 potential mates and success means finding the single best.
The goal remains the single best among 100 candidates.
The first 14 percent must all become partners.
entries.promptZh: 在什么条件下，先看 14% 的成功概率最高？
optionsZh: 100 个候选，成功目标是优质选项之一。
1,000 个候选，目标是唯一最优者。
100 个候选，目标仍是唯一最优者。
前 14% 必须全成为伴侣。

entries.prompt: What procedure is described for 100 potential mates?
options: Reject all candidates after examining the first 14.
Choose the best of the first 14 retrospectively.
Select exactly the fourteenth candidate regardless of quality.
Examine the first 14, then choose the next candidate who exceeds their best.
entries.promptZh: 100 个潜在对象时，片段描述什么步骤？
optionsZh: 考察前 14 个后拒绝所有人。
回头选择前 14 个中最好的。
不论质量直接选第 14 个。
考察前 14 个，再选随后超过其中最佳者的对象。

entries.prompt: Which statement restates the rule for 1,000 potential mates?
options: Choose one of the first 30 without comparing later candidates.
Use the best of the first 30 as a benchmark for a subsequent choice.
Wait until all 1,000 have been considered before choosing.
Treat the first 30 as the only acceptable partners.
entries.promptZh: 哪项准确改述 1,000 个候选时的规则？
optionsZh: 不比较后来对象，直接选前 30 个之一。
以前 30 个中最好者为基准，选择后来的对象。
看完全部 1,000 个才选择。
只有前 30 个才可接受。

entries.prompt: Why does the author ask about twelve serious relationships?
options: To report that twelve relationships guarantee a successful marriage.
To show that apartments and partners have identical search costs.
To question whether a simpler heuristic can still be difficult in practice.
To claim that Todd and Miller require exactly twelve marriages.
entries.promptZh: 作者为何追问怎样拥有十二段认真交往？
optionsZh: 报告十二段关系保证婚姻成功。
表明找房和择偶成本完全一样。
质疑较简单的经验规则在现实中仍可能很难。
称两研究者要求恰好十二次婚姻。

entries.prompt: How does Kepler’s search compare with the “take a dozen” heuristic?
options: His eleven candidates were close to the suggested dozen.
He considered twelve candidates every year.
He evaluated only two candidates over eleven years.
His search exactly matched twelve candidates in two months.
entries.promptZh: Kepler 的搜索与“考察一打”规则怎样比较？
optionsZh: 十一名候选接近建议的一打。
每年考察十二名。
十一年仅考察两名。
两个月恰好考察十二名。

entries.prompt: What question organizes this short passage?
options: How to calculate a new exact search percentage.
Whether all decisions have already been experimentally solved.
Why rejection never affects real choices.
What besides cost and possible rejection may explain limited exploration.
entries.promptZh: 本短段围绕什么问题？
optionsZh: 如何计算新的精确搜索比例。
是否所有决策都已被实验解决。
为何拒绝从不影响选择。
成本和拒绝风险之外，什么解释探索不足。

entries.prompt: What did Bossard examine in the marriage licenses?
options: How satisfied each couple was after fifty years.
Where each partner had lived when applying.
Whether online dating caused their marriage.
The number of rejected proposals per applicant.
entries.promptZh: Bossard 在结婚许可资料中考察什么？
optionsZh: 五十年后婚姻满意度。
双方提出申请时住在哪里。
网恋是否导致结婚。
每位申请者求婚被拒次数。

entries.prompt: Which numerical statement accurately describes the findings?
options: 82.2 percent had lived together before marriage.
17.8 percent had both lived outside Philadelphia.
Over half had lived within twenty blocks of each other.
33.58 percent had lived more than twenty blocks apart.
entries.promptZh: 哪项数字描述符合结果？
optionsZh: 82.2% 婚前已同居。
17.8% 双方均住市外。
超过一半婚前相距不超过二十个街区。
33.58% 相距超过二十个街区。

entries.prompt: What does Bossard’s comment about Cupid’s wings illustrate?
options: Partners often came from a restricted local area despite many possible candidates.
The study measured the actual flight distance of birds.
Most couples deliberately compared every candidate in the city.
The city offered very few potential partners in total.
entries.promptZh: Bossard 关于丘比特翅膀的评论说明什么？
optionsZh: 虽有众多潜在人选，伴侣常来自有限的邻近区域。
研究测量鸟的实际飞行距离。
多数夫妇刻意比较过全市每个候选。
全市潜在伴侣总数极少。

entries.prompt: Why should proximity in 1931 Philadelphia not be treated as an isolated explanation?
options: Residents had been randomly allocated to all neighborhoods.
Distance was measured only after marriage.
Shared backgrounds were explicitly ruled out.
Nearby residence could also reflect shared backgrounds and more opportunities to interact.
entries.promptZh: 为何不能把 1931 年费城的近距离当成孤立解释？
optionsZh: 居民已被随机分配至所有街区。
只在结婚后量距离。
共同背景被明确排除。
住得近也可能反映共同背景和更多接触机会。

entries.prompt: Which statement best restates this sentence?
options: Nearby residents inevitably became close friends.
People living close together were much more likely to become acquainted.
Distant residents were more likely to meet by chance.
Acquaintanceship determined everyone’s exact address.
entries.promptZh: 哪项最准确改述此句？
optionsZh: 近邻必定成为密友。
住得近的人相识的可能性大得多。
远处居民更可能偶遇。
相识决定每个人的具体住址。

entries.prompt: Why does the author introduce the objection that the study was conducted in 1931?
options: To invite consideration of whether findings transfer across changing social conditions.
To announce that the original licenses were fabricated.
To show that cross-religious marriage was then the norm.
To establish that where people live has remained unchanged.
entries.promptZh: 作者为何引入“那可是 1931 年”的异议？
optionsZh: 引导考虑社会条件改变后结果是否仍适用。
宣布原许可系伪造。
说明当时跨宗教婚姻是常态。
确立居住方式从未变化。

entries.prompt: What is the function of the question about the residential proximity effect?
options: It confirms that online dating has eliminated proximity.
It denies any increase in the apparent pool of partners.
It asks whether an apparent expansion of choice has made proximity outdated.
It measures the exact rate of growth in online users.
entries.promptZh: 关于居住邻近效应的问句起什么作用？
optionsZh: 确认网恋已消除邻近影响。
否认潜在对象看来有所增加。
追问选择范围似乎扩大后，邻近影响是否已过时。
测量网民增长的精确速率。

entries.prompt: Who was specifically selected for the Dutch study?
options: 289,248 newly married couples from all European countries.
Every Dutch citizen regardless of relationship status or year.
Only people who met through online dating platforms.
289,248 individuals who began cohabiting as domestic partners during 2004.
entries.promptZh: 荷兰研究具体选取了谁？
optionsZh: 欧洲各国 289,248 对新婚夫妻。
不论关系和年份的每位荷兰公民。
只选在线平台认识的人。
2004 年开始以伴侣身份同居的 289,248 名个人。

entries.prompt: Why did researchers also examine addresses roughly five years earlier?
options: Some applicants might already have been living together when submitting their application.
Earlier addresses were guaranteed to reveal each person’s birthplace.
The application records contained no residential information.
All partners had separated exactly five years before applying.
entries.promptZh: 为何还考察约五年前的住址？
optionsZh: 部分申请者提出申请时可能已经同居。
早期住址保证等于出生地。
申请记录完全没有住址信息。
所有伴侣都在申请前恰好五年分开。

entries.prompt: Which statement correctly interprets the reported distances?
options: One kilometer was the median distance at birth.
The median distance at birth was 22.9 kilometers.
Thirteen percent had lived one kilometer apart five years earlier.
Every couple had lived less than fifteen miles apart before cohabitation.
entries.promptZh: 哪项正确理解所报距离？
optionsZh: 出生地距离中位数是一公里。
出生地之间距离中位数为 22.9 公里。
五年前相距一公里者占 13%。
每对伴侣同居前都相距不到十五英里。

entries.prompt: What does the comparison with Cupid in Philadelphia suggest?
options: Every Dutch partner in 2004 had met online.
The Internet had proved incapable of forming any relationship.
Geographical closeness still characterized partnerships in the Dutch data.
The two studies measured exactly the same distance percentages.
entries.promptZh: 与费城丘比特的比较提示什么？
optionsZh: 2004 年所有荷兰伴侣都在网上认识。
互联网被证明不能形成任何关系。
荷兰数据中的伴侣配对仍有地理邻近特征。
两研究测得完全相同的距离百分比。

entries.prompt: Why was the selection effect minimized in the MIT setting?
options: Unlike Philadelphia, the complexes lacked ethnic enclaves that attracted particular groups.
Researchers required all residents to choose the same three friends.
The study excluded every resident born outside the city.
Every resident was allowed to select a neighborhood by religion.
entries.promptZh: MIT 场景为何使选择效应减小？
optionsZh: 不同于费城，公寓群没有吸引特定群体的族裔聚居区。
研究者要求大家选同样三个朋友。
排除了所有外地出生居民。
每人可按宗教自选社区。

entries.prompt: What does the figure of 112 out of 187 refer to?
options: Participants who had exactly three next-door friends.
Residents who lived four or more units away from everyone.
Couples who had applied for marriage licenses.
Friendship nominations involving someone next door or directly linked by stairs.
entries.promptZh: 112/187 这个数字指什么？
optionsZh: 恰有三个隔壁朋友的参与者。
与所有人都相隔四个单元以上的居民。
申请结婚许可的夫妇。
被提名朋友住隔壁或在楼梯直接连通单元的提名。

entries.prompt: What does functional distance help explain here?
options: Why floor numbers alone perfectly predict every friendship.
Why everyone near stairs becomes friends immediately.
Why convenient routes can increase informal encounters and friendship opportunities.
Why physical distance ceases to matter near staircases.
entries.promptZh: 这里的功能距离帮助解释什么？
optionsZh: 仅靠楼层号码便能完美预测每段友谊。
为何楼梯旁的人马上全成朋友。
方便的动线为何增加非正式相遇与交友机会。
为何楼梯附近物理距离就无关紧要。

entries.prompt: What is the purpose of the final question?
options: To move from the pattern of chance encounters to a question about its mechanism.
To deny that geography has any power in dormitories.
To claim all residents share identical religious beliefs.
To introduce a measured effect of online dating platforms.
entries.promptZh: 末尾问题有什么作用？
optionsZh: 从偶遇与关系的模式转向追问机制。
否认地理在宿舍中的影响。
声称所有居民宗教信仰相同。
引入网恋平台的实测效果。

entries.prompt: What research sequence does the author describe?
options: Observe a correlation and immediately declare it causal.
Identify a real-world association, then test possible causal mechanisms.
Reject all field observations before examining any variables.
Treat familiarity as identical to residential distance.
entries.promptZh: 作者描述了怎样的研究顺序？
optionsZh: 观察相关后马上宣布因果。
先识别现实关联，再检验可能的因果机制。
考察变量前拒绝全部实地观察。
把熟悉感等同居住距离。

entries.prompt: How was word desirability determined in the earlier work?
options: By counting printed occurrences without asking any speakers.
By measuring how long words took to pronounce.
By checking whether words came from Turkish.
By combining English speakers’ ratings of English words.
entries.promptZh: 早期研究如何确定词语的讨喜程度？
optionsZh: 不问说话者，只数印刷出现次数。
测量发音所需时间。
检查词是否来自土耳其语。
汇总英语使用者对英语词语的评分。

entries.prompt: Why might “good” be rated more desirable than “better” in the reported task?
options: It has a more positive dictionary meaning.
It is encountered more frequently in use.
It was the only word participants knew.
It had fewer printed appearances.
entries.promptZh: 为什么所报任务中 good 可能比 better 更讨喜？
optionsZh: 字典意义更积极。
使用中出现得更频繁。
参与者只认识这一个词。
印刷出现次数更少。

entries.prompt: Why did Zajonc move from word-frequency findings to a new experiment?
options: Earlier findings proved that frequency had no effect.
The earlier words were all genuinely Turkish.
A correlation alone could not establish a causal effect.
Pronunciation had already explained every rating.
entries.promptZh: Zajonc 为什么从词频发现转向新实验？
optionsZh: 早期发现证明频率无效。
早期词全部是真土耳其语。
仅有相关不能确立因果效应。
发音已解释全部评分。

entries.prompt: How was familiarity manipulated in this task?
options: By presenting different words different numbers of times.
By teaching participants accurate Turkish translations.
By showing every word exactly twelve times.
By letting participants choose their own exposure frequency.
entries.promptZh: 任务怎样操纵熟悉度？
optionsZh: 使不同词出现不同次数。
教准确土耳其语翻译。
每词恰好呈现十二次。
让参与者自选呈现次数。

entries.prompt: What pattern was replicated across the materials described?
options: Chinese characters were always preferred to photographs.
All photographs received identical ratings.
Only real words benefited from repetition.
More frequent presentation increased positive evaluations of the same stimuli.
entries.promptZh: 不同材料中重复出现什么结果模式？
optionsZh: 汉字总比照片受欢迎。
所有照片评分相同。
只有真实词重复后才受益。
同一刺激呈现更频繁时，正面评价更高。

entries.prompt: Which feature distinguished the four women’s participation in the classroom experiment?
options: They attended different subjects at different universities.
They attended the same course with different frequencies.
They were selected to differ greatly in attractiveness.
Each attended all lectures throughout the semester.
entries.promptZh: 四名女性在课堂实验中的参与有什么差别？
optionsZh: 在不同大学上不同科目。
同一课程的出席频率不同。
专门挑选外貌吸引力差很多的人。
每个人整个学期全勤。

entries.prompt: Why were the assistants instructed to use the same staircases and seating area?
options: To ensure that they never became visible.
To test differences in formal clothing.
To make them visible to most students in a similar way.
To require them to talk to every student.
entries.promptZh: 为何要求助理走相同楼梯、坐同一区域？
optionsZh: 确保始终不可见。
测试正装差异。
让大多数学生以相似方式看见她们。
要求与每位学生谈话。

entries.prompt: Which dimension were students asked to rate at the semester’s end?
options: How similar each woman seemed to themselves.
The women’s examination results.
How many lectures the students themselves missed.
Each assistant’s actual family background.
entries.promptZh: 学期末要求学生评哪个维度？
optionsZh: 每名女性看起来与自己有多相似。
女性的考试成绩。
学生自己缺课次数。
每位助理的实际家庭背景。

entries.prompt: Which pairing of attendance and attractiveness rating is correct?
options: No attendance: 4.38.
Five attendances: 4.25.
Ten attendances: 3.62.
Fifteen attendances: 4.38.
entries.promptZh: 哪组出席次数和吸引力评分对应正确？

entries.prompt: What distinction does the passage draw about awareness?
options: Everyone explicitly recognized all four women.
Positive exposure effects may appear without much explicit recognition.
Nobody had ever seen any of the women.
Students rated objective similarity instead of perceived similarity.
entries.promptZh: 片段对意识作出什么区分？
optionsZh: 所有人明确认出四人。
曝光影响可能在缺乏明确认出的情况下出现。
没有人曾看过任何一人。
学生评客观相似性而非主观感受。

entries.prompt: Which women received higher familiarity ratings in this comparison?
options: Those who attended five times rather than fifteen.
Only the woman who never attended.
Those who attended ten or fifteen times.
All four received the same ratings.
entries.promptZh: 比较中哪些女性的熟悉度评分更高？
optionsZh: 五次比十五次者高。
只有从没来者高。
出席十次或十五次者。
四人评分相同。

entries.prompt: How does the author connect the experiments to the earlier geographical studies?
options: The experiments offer a causal mechanism involving familiarity, similarity and favorability.
The geographical studies had randomly assigned every marriage.
Repeated exposure reduces all perceived similarity.
The experiments prove that proximity guarantees marriage.
entries.promptZh: 作者怎样将实验与此前地理研究联系起来？
optionsZh: 实验提供涉及熟悉感、相似感和好感的因果机制解释。
地理研究随机分配了每段婚姻。
重复曝光降低所有相似感。
实验证明近距离保证结婚。

entries.prompt: Which statement preserves the qualification in this sentence?
options: Every repeated meeting inevitably leads to romance.
Chance meetings eliminate attraction over time.
Only romantic partners ever meet by chance.
Repeated chance meetings can strengthen attraction and occasionally develop into romance.
entries.promptZh: 哪项保留此句的限定？
optionsZh: 每次重复相遇必成恋情。
偶遇逐渐消除吸引。
只有恋人才会偶遇。
反复偶遇能增强吸引，有时发展成恋情。

entries.prompt: Why does the author introduce his visits to two shopping malls?
options: To report a randomized comparison of store sizes.
To open a new question about exposure effects beyond interpersonal relationships.
To establish that smaller malls contain more stores.
To prove that all American cities are objectively identical.
entries.promptZh: 作者为何引入逛两个商场的经历？
optionsZh: 报告商场大小随机比较。
引出人际关系之外曝光效应的新问题。
确立小商场商店更多。
证明美国所有城市客观相同。

entries.prompt: What puzzled the author about the two malls?
options: They were both in Staten Island.
Neither contained any familiar stores.
They looked alike and contained many of the same stores.
They had exactly the same measured floor area.
entries.promptZh: 两个商场的什么让作者困惑？
optionsZh: 两者都在 Staten Island。
都没有熟悉店铺。
看着相同，许多店铺也相同。
实测面积完全一样。

entries.prompt: What does “cookie-cutter” suggest about the housing developments?
options: They look standardized and much like one another.
They are designed mainly for professional bakers.
They are unique to each conference attendee.
They are located inside airport terminals.
entries.promptZh: cookie-cutter 暗示住宅开发区什么特点？
optionsZh: 标准化、彼此很像。
主要为烘焙师设计。
每位参会者各有独特版本。
位于机场航站楼内。

entries.prompt: What contrast does the author draw between Japan and American suburbs?
options: Tokyo and Osaka have no large buildings or stations.
All Japanese stores belong to American chains.
American suburbs contain no restaurants.
Japanese cities can feel distinct despite shared urban features, unlike the repeated chains he describes in U.S. suburbs.
entries.promptZh: 作者对日本与美国郊区作什么对比？
optionsZh: 东京大阪没有大楼车站。
日本商店全属美国连锁。
美国郊区没有餐厅。
日本城市虽有共同大都市设施仍感觉不同，而所述美国郊区反复出现连锁店。

entries.prompt: How did the author’s responses change when he travelled?
options: He avoided Starbucks both at home and away.
He welcomed familiar stores and people more warmly away from home.
He greeted the student more curtly in Las Vegas.
He visited Starbucks every day in Charlottesville.
entries.promptZh: 旅行时作者的反应怎样变化？
optionsZh: 在家出门都避开 Starbucks。
出门时更热情地欢迎熟悉店铺和熟人。
在 Las Vegas 更冷淡招呼学生。
在 Charlottesville 天天去 Starbucks。

entries.prompt: What tentative explanation follows the author’s near-hug?
options: He habitually hugged Gary in Gilmer Hall.
Strangers become less noticeable in familiar places.
Familiar people or stores may seem especially attractive amid unfamiliar surroundings.
Every traveller always embraces familiar students.
entries.promptZh: 差点拥抱之后，作者提出什么初步解释？
